The data presented herein covers the period of January 1 through December 31, 2025 (Calendar Year 2025).
Total aggregate payments received ($812.9 million) exceed aggregate acquisition costs ($399.1 million), yielding a gross program margin of approximately $413.7 million.

For Calendar Year 2025, Idaho covered entities collectively reported nearly 1.92 million prescription drugs obtained under the 340B program and dispensed to patients, generating over $812.9 million in aggregate payments received, while directing $430.6 million in 340B savings toward charity care, community benefit programs, and services for indigent patients.

For CY2025, the total aggregate acquisition cost across all Idaho covered entities was $399,146,308.13.
For CY2025, the total aggregate payments received by all Idaho 340B covered entities was $812,855,944.90.
For CY2025, Idaho covered entities made total aggregate payments to contract pharmacies of $46,157,188.85.
For CY2025, Idaho covered entities collectively reported 1,916,995 total claims across all payer categories.
Commercial insurance was the dominant payer category, accounting for 45.4% of all claims, followed by Medicare at 31.1%.
For CY2025, Idaho covered entities directed a total of $430,646,950.35 in 340B savings.

answer_as_filed: Trinity Hospital Twin City is a small critical access hospital located in Dennison, Ohio, and is approximately 20 minutes away from the next closest institution that provides similar services. We are located in a federally designated Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA). Despite operating at a loss, Twin City provides over $1.4 million in community benefits including direct financial assistance and unreimbursed Medicaid care. The 340B program is crucial to the health of our community. We use our 340B savings to teach healthy life choices through our Fit for Life Program, which aims to reduce the number of overweight and obese men and women of all ages in Tuscarawas County and the surrounding counties of Carroll, Guernsey, and Harrison. We also provide support for the community through our Diabetes Wellness program. Twin City also provides medication assistance through its contract pharmacy arrangements that allows qualified patients to receive drugs at discounted prices.

answer_as_filed:
"Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B Drug Pricing Program to continue to provide the highest quality care for the communities we serve. By lowering the cost of eligible outpatient medications, 340B helps us redirect resources into patient care, pharmacy access and essential services for people who might otherwise have limited access to treatment. For Cleveland Clinic, 340B helps us stretch limited resources so we can continue serving as a safety net for highly specialized care, while also supporting patients experiencing unmet needs.
Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B benefit to help provide access to care, preserve access points and reinvest in broader community health efforts. In 2024 alone (the most recent year for which complete data are available), we provided $337.7 million in free or discounted care to more than 139,000 patients, contributed $1.49 billion in community benefit across Ohio, Florida and Nevada, and provided $28.7 million in subsidized health services that meet important community needs despite operating at a loss.
340B also helps Cleveland Clinic maintain pharmacy access and reduce barriers to medication adherence. Examples include operating 27 retail pharmacy locations across Northeast Ohio, opening a new community pharmacy at South Pointe Hospital in 2025, delivering, at no delivery cost, discharge prescriptions to patients and providing transition-of-care pharmacist support for patients after discharge.
For more information on how Cleveland Clinic uses 340B savings please visit our website at https://my.clevelandclinic.org/about/community/reports/340b-program
"

340B savings help support University Hospitals’ overall capacity to provide community benefit, which totaled $511 million in 2024. These resources play an important role in sustaining a wide range of programs and services that benefit our patients and community. These supports include:

Financial assistance for patients who are unable to afford hospital care, physician care and/or medications
Medication access services to help patients navigate insurance requirements and reduce financial barriers
Patient engagement programs focused on refill management and improving adherence to therapy
Clinical services, including pharmacists embedded in provider offices and ongoing care management
Education and training by preparing future generations of caregivers
Transportation assistance
Home health services
Community outreach initiatives
Medicaid shortfall and other uncompensated care
Support for medical research
In-kind contributions to community organizations

answer_as_filed:
340B savings help support University Hospitals’ overall capacity to provide community benefit, which totaled $511 million in 2024. These resources play an important role in sustaining a wide range of programs and services that benefit our patients and community. These supports include:

Financial assistance for patients who are unable to afford hospital care, physician care and/or medications
Medication access services to help patients navigate insurance requirements and reduce financial barriers
Patient engagement programs focused on refill management and improving adherence to therapy
Clinical services, including pharmacists embedded in provider offices and ongoing care management
Education and training by preparing future generations of caregivers
Transportation assistance
Home health services
Community outreach initiatives
Medicaid shortfall and other uncompensated care
Support for medical research
In-kind contributions to community organizations

answer_as_filed: Harrison Community Hospital (HCH) is a 25-bed Critical Access Hospital in Cadiz, Ohio, serving Harrison County and the surrounding tri-state region for more than 50 years. The 340B Drug Pricing Program enables HCH to maximize limited resources and reinvest savings into programs and services that support low-income, uninsured, underinsured, homeless, and rural patients. HCH offers a broad range of healthcare services, including: 24-hour emergency care, surgical services, diagnostic imaging, inpatient and outpatient laboratory services, rehabilitation and therapy services, swing bed care, outpatient infusion services and primary care.

In 2024, 340B savings offset 17.9% of Harrison Community Hospital's total charity care, uncompensated care, and bad debt expense. While these savings are critical to sustaining access to care, the hospital continues to absorb most of these costs as part of its mission to serve all patients, regardless of their ability to pay. While 340B savings support these efforts, the hospital continues to provide significant levels of charity and uncompensated care beyond the resources generated through the program. These investments reflect HCH's ongoing commitment to improving the health and well-being of the communities it serves through quality care, expanded access to services, and support for healthcare workforce development.
340B program savings are reinvested in three key areas:
Charity Care – Providing financial assistance to patients who are unable to afford healthcare services.
Facility Improvements – Maintaining and upgrading facilities and equipment to support a safe, high-quality care environment.
Service Preservation – Sustaining essential healthcare services locally, reducing the need for uninsured and underserved patients to travel long distances for care.

Our 340B Story

About Avita Health System

Avita Health System is a nonprofit, patient-centered health care system in North Central Ohio. It was established in 2011 as the parent company of Bucyrus and Galion Hospitals. In 2017, Avita opened its third hospital, located in Ontario, and now has over 40 clinics and service locations in Crawford and Richland counties with more than 150 employed medical providers, 1,000 affiliated medical providers, and 2,400 employees. Avita services 9 counties with populations totaling over 500,000 Ohioans. Avita’s mission is to improve the health and well-being of those we serve by providing exceptional patient experiences across the continuum of care and consistently exceeding national benchmarks for quality, care, and service.  Unique to the area, Avita is an independent, locally governed health care system with a board of directors that live in the communities where health services are provided.  As a nonprofit health system, Avita values charitable giving and provided over $48 million in uncompensated, unreimbursed, and charity care in FY2025. 

Benefits of the 340B Program

Avita Health System relies on the 340B Drug Pricing Program in order to “stretch scarce Federal resources as far as possible, reaching more eligible patients and providing more comprehensive care”, as Congress had originally intended.  The 340B program is funded entirely through drug manufacturer discounts and there is no cost to the taxpayer or community.  The 340B program is critical to ensuring Avita’s role as a safety-net community hospital, thereby providing vital access to comprehensive and life-saving health services, programs, and prescription drugs.  Savings realized through participation in the 340B program are reinvested into Avita Health System’s internal programs and services, or the expansion of external community assistance programs.  These programs and services include, but are not limited to:

The 340B program enables Avita Health System to expand access to medications across the continuum of care. 
•	Maintaining formulary access to critical medications that, without 340B discounts, could not be sustainably offered due to reimbursement rates below acquisition costs
•	Patient access to ultra high cost specialty pharmaceuticals and infusions, including immunotherapy, bispecifics, and radioligand therapy at our infusion centers and comprehensive cancer center
•	Subsidizing chemotherapy and immunotherapy for uninsured and underinsured patients
•	Providing pediatric vaccines at all pediatrician and family medicine physician practices system-wide, including continuing a neonatal Hepatitis B vaccination program that provides the birth dose at no charge to patients 
•	Expanding access to outpatient pharmacy services through a second entity-owned retail pharmacy in Crestline, Ohio, restoring essential pharmaceutical care to a community that had become a pharmacy desert. 

The 340B Program enables Avita Health System to stretch scarce federal resources as far as possible, reaching more eligible patients and providing more comprehensive services.

•	Maintaining community access to 24/7 critical services including emergency medicine (ER), inpatient care, surgery, advanced imaging, and intensive care at all three Avita Health System hospitals
•	Continuing our commitment to women’s health and perinatal care by continuing to provide Maternity & Obstetric services in Crawford County, while expanding services in Richland County 
•	Expanding access to specialized services and medical expertise, such as cardiac catheterization, inpatient hemodialysis/CRRT, and telestroke medicine 
•	Providing critical support for ICU and Med/Surg patients with pulmonologists, intensivists, nephrologists, neurologists, cardiologists, and other specialists that enable patients to receive care close to home, without transferring out of the system. 
•	Expanding outpatient access to specialty medical and surgical services in our rural, Critical Access Hospitals, including rheumatology, urology, orthopedics, spinal surgery, gastroenterology, pain management, ENT, and wound care (including hyperbaric oxygen treatment) allowing patients to receive expert care close to home
•	Access to adult and pediatric occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech therapy and audiology services
•	Expanding access to state-of-the-art technology, including robotic surgery, 3D mammography, 3T MRI, and LINAC with RapidArc® Dynamic planning.
•	Expanding cancer care for our communities through medical oncology and infusion services at all three Avita Heath System hospitals and a new, state-of-the-art comprehensive Cancer Center in Richland County offering radiation oncology services in addition to medical oncology and infusion. 
•	Nurse navigation services for oncology patients to guide them through their cancer care journey
•	Access to charity and indigent care programs, as well as financial assistance for basic medical services, oncology and other specialty medications
•	Access to patient billing advocates and financial counselors to assist with needs beyond direct medical care, such as gas, electricity, transportation, etc.
•	Absorbing waived self-administered drug charges for Medicare observation patients
•	Outpatient social work services to support patients with psychosocial needs and care coordination
•	Access to psychiatric and addiction medicine services for patients with mental health and substance use disorders.
•	Crisis intervention services for patients experiencing mental health or behavioral health emergencies
•	Access to full service Home Health and Hospice care across an 8 county region, including inpatient hospice and respite care. 
•	Providing ambulatory clinical pharmacy services (Medication Therapy Management clinics) to at-risk patients to improve medication adherence and outcomes through disease state management
•	Expanding access to patient assistance programs through pharmacist coordinated Medication Access Programs and Drug Repository Services 
•	Partnerships with local communities to provide community health improvement services, such as diabetes prevention, prenatal support, and tobacco cessation
•	Offer free sports physicals for the community and access to athletic training services to school districts in local and surrounding counties
•	Sensory kits for neurodivergent pediatric patients in the Emergency Department to support their comfort and care experience
•	24/7 access to forensic services, including free medical screenings and exams for victims of sexual assault and abuse, child abuse, domestic violence, human trafficking, and other criminal offenses for victims in Crawford, Richland, and surrounding counties. 
•	Access to 365 day Walk In Clinic services at 3 separate locations across Richland county.
•	Access to pre-employment evaluations, post-accident services, and training programs for local employers through our WorkWell Occupational Health services.
•	Staff tuition assistance and subsidy programs to support continuing education and professional development
•	Nurse education partnerships with local nursing schools, enabling staff to complete nursing school at no cost to them, strengthening our workforce and community

Impact of Scaling back the 340B Program

Avita Health System is committed to our mission of improving the health and wellbeing of those we serve. We fulfill our mission primarily through the services and programs that we offer our patients, as well as through the support that we give to our communities. Scaling back the 340B Program would threaten our capacity to maintain access to the full scope of medications and services described above, jeopardizing essential care in our rural communities where healthcare options are already limited.

answer_as_filed: Barnesville Hospital is a 25-bed critical access hospital serving an economically challenged Appalachian region in southeastern Ohio. Since joining the West Virginia University Health System on April 1, 2021, the hospital has continued to provide essential healthcare services to residents across multiple counties, including a neighboring county that lacks a hospital of its own. The region's population is older than the national average, and many residents face significant economic barriers, with a substantial percentage living below the federal poverty level.

The 340B Drug Pricing Program plays a vital role in helping Barnesville Hospital maximize limited resources while maintaining access to high-quality healthcare services for vulnerable populations. These include low-income, uninsured, underinsured, and homeless individuals, as well as residents of rural communities who often face challenges in accessing care. By reinvesting program savings into clinical services, infrastructure, and community health initiatives, the hospital has improved patient outcomes and strengthened its ability to serve those most in need.
According to the 2024 Impact Report, savings generated through the 340B Program have been reinvested in several key areas that directly benefit patients and the community:
Charity Care: Expanding access to care for patients who are unable to afford medical services.
Clinic Expansion: Supporting the development of two additional Family Medicine Clinics to improve access to primary care.
Patient Safety and Facility Improvements: Funding infrastructure enhancements, pharmacy staffing, and medication reconciliation initiatives that strengthen patient safety and quality of care.
Capital Equipment Purchases: Acquiring essential patient care equipment, including new hospital beds not covered by federal grant funding.

Our 340B Story

About Avita Health System

Avita Health System is a nonprofit, patient-centered health care system in North Central Ohio. It was established in 2011 as the parent company of Bucyrus and Galion Hospitals. In 2017, Avita opened its third hospital, located in Ontario, and now has over 40 clinics and service locations in Crawford and Richland counties with more than 150 employed medical providers, 1,000 affiliated medical providers, and 2,400 employees. Avita services 9 counties with populations totaling over 500,000 Ohioans. Avita’s mission is to improve the health and well-being of those we serve by providing exceptional patient experiences across the continuum of care and consistently exceeding national benchmarks for quality, care, and service.  Unique to the area, Avita is an independent, locally governed health care system with a board of directors that live in the communities where health services are provided.  As a nonprofit health system, Avita values charitable giving and provided over $48 million in uncompensated, unreimbursed, and charity care in FY2025. 

Benefits of the 340B Program

Avita Health System relies on the 340B Drug Pricing Program in order to “stretch scarce Federal resources as far as possible, reaching more eligible patients and providing more comprehensive care”, as Congress had originally intended.  The 340B program is funded entirely through drug manufacturer discounts and there is no cost to the taxpayer or community.  The 340B program is critical to ensuring Avita’s role as a safety-net community hospital, thereby providing vital access to comprehensive and life-saving health services, programs, and prescription drugs.  Savings realized through participation in the 340B program are reinvested into Avita Health System’s internal programs and services, or the expansion of external community assistance programs.  These programs and services include, but are not limited to:

The 340B program enables Avita Health System to expand access to medications across the continuum of care. 
•	Maintaining formulary access to critical medications that, without 340B discounts, could not be sustainably offered due to reimbursement rates below acquisition costs
•	Patient access to ultra high cost specialty pharmaceuticals and infusions, including immunotherapy, bispecifics, and radioligand therapy at our infusion centers and comprehensive cancer center
•	Subsidizing chemotherapy and immunotherapy for uninsured and underinsured patients
•	Providing pediatric vaccines at all pediatrician and family medicine physician practices system-wide, including continuing a neonatal Hepatitis B vaccination program that provides the birth dose at no charge to patients 
•	Expanding access to outpatient pharmacy services through a second entity-owned retail pharmacy in Crestline, Ohio, restoring essential pharmaceutical care to a community that had become a pharmacy desert. 

The 340B Program enables Avita Health System to stretch scarce federal resources as far as possible, reaching more eligible patients and providing more comprehensive services.

•	Maintaining community access to 24/7 critical services including emergency medicine (ER), inpatient care, surgery, advanced imaging, and intensive care at all three Avita Health System hospitals
•	Continuing our commitment to women’s health and perinatal care by continuing to provide Maternity & Obstetric services in Crawford County, while expanding services in Richland County 
•	Expanding access to specialized services and medical expertise, such as cardiac catheterization, inpatient hemodialysis/CRRT, and telestroke medicine 
•	Providing critical support for ICU and Med/Surg patients with pulmonologists, intensivists, nephrologists, neurologists, cardiologists, and other specialists that enable patients to receive care close to home, without transferring out of the system. 
•	Expanding outpatient access to specialty medical and surgical services in our rural, Critical Access Hospitals, including rheumatology, urology, orthopedics, spinal surgery, gastroenterology, pain management, ENT, and wound care (including hyperbaric oxygen treatment) allowing patients to receive expert care close to home
•	Access to adult and pediatric occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech therapy and audiology services
•	Expanding access to state-of-the-art technology, including robotic surgery, 3D mammography, 3T MRI, and LINAC with RapidArc® Dynamic planning.
•	Expanding cancer care for our communities through medical oncology and infusion services at all three Avita Heath System hospitals and a new, state-of-the-art comprehensive Cancer Center in Richland County offering radiation oncology services in addition to medical oncology and infusion. 
•	Nurse navigation services for oncology patients to guide them through their cancer care journey
•	Access to charity and indigent care programs, as well as financial assistance for basic medical services, oncology and other specialty medications
•	Access to patient billing advocates and financial counselors to assist with needs beyond direct medical care, such as gas, electricity, transportation, etc.
•	Absorbing waived self-administered drug charges for Medicare observation patients
•	Outpatient social work services to support patients with psychosocial needs and care coordination
•	Access to psychiatric and addiction medicine services for patients with mental health and substance use disorders.
•	Crisis intervention services for patients experiencing mental health or behavioral health emergencies
•	Access to full service Home Health and Hospice care across an 8 county region, including inpatient hospice and respite care. 
•	Providing ambulatory clinical pharmacy services (Medication Therapy Management clinics) to at-risk patients to improve medication adherence and outcomes through disease state management
•	Expanding access to patient assistance programs through pharmacist coordinated Medication Access Programs and Drug Repository Services 
•	Partnerships with local communities to provide community health improvement services, such as diabetes prevention, prenatal support, and tobacco cessation
•	Offer free sports physicals for the community and access to athletic training services to school districts in local and surrounding counties
•	Sensory kits for neurodivergent pediatric patients in the Emergency Department to support their comfort and care experience
•	24/7 access to forensic services, including free medical screenings and exams for victims of sexual assault and abuse, child abuse, domestic violence, human trafficking, and other criminal offenses for victims in Crawford, Richland, and surrounding counties. 
•	Access to 365 day Walk In Clinic services at 3 separate locations across Richland county.
•	Access to pre-employment evaluations, post-accident services, and training programs for local employers through our WorkWell Occupational Health services.
•	Staff tuition assistance and subsidy programs to support continuing education and professional development
•	Nurse education partnerships with local nursing schools, enabling staff to complete nursing school at no cost to them, strengthening our workforce and community

Impact of Scaling back the 340B Program

Avita Health System is committed to our mission of improving the health and wellbeing of those we serve. We fulfill our mission primarily through the services and programs that we offer our patients, as well as through the support that we give to our communities. Scaling back the 340B Program would threaten our capacity to maintain access to the full scope of medications and services described above, jeopardizing essential care in our rural communities where healthcare options are already limited.

answer_as_filed: CHWC-Montpelier reported to CMS $1,305,874 in unreimbursed care (line 31 in cost report), of which $218,274 was charity care. Across all of Parkview Health’s 340B covered entities in Indiana, Parkview reported more than $143 million in unreimbursed care. Additionally, last year, Parkview Health partnered with Undue Medical Debt to abolish $64.13 million in debt for 35,694 patients.

CHWC-Montpelier participates in the 340B Drug Pricing Program and reinvests program savings to support access to care, improve clinical services, and reduce financial barriers for vulnerable and underserved patient populations. These investments are directed toward patient‑facing services and system capabilities that align with the program’s statutory intent.
Subsidized health services at CHWC-Montpelier include ambulance/EMS, hospice, outpatient rehab, neonatology, and other services.

Community benefit investments (as reported on IRS form 990 schedule H 2024) across all of Parkview Health’s 340B covered entities in Indiana surpassed $36 million for community health services that are not billed - Examples across Parkview Health include childbirth classes, postpartum support, diabetes education, mobile health services, cystic fibrosis intervention, blood pressure clinics, and additional services.

Savings are also reinvested at Parkview Health in a broad range of clinical services that improve quality, safety, and continuity of care. These include acute and outpatient clinical services, chronic disease management programs, outpatient infusion services, and pharmacist‑led programs such as medication therapy management, prior authorization support, immunization programs, and antibiotic stewardship. Parkview also supports preventive care, community wellness initiatives, and behavioral health services. Research and innovation programs are included to advance care delivery and outcomes.

Parkview uses 340B savings to directly reduce patient out‑of‑pocket costs and support medication affordability. This includes a robust pharmacy-managed, means-tested patient assistance program. This is intended to promote medication adherence and continuity of care for financially vulnerable patients.

Savings are also applied to provider education initiatives, including physician, nursing, and pharmacy training programs, to support a well‑prepared healthcare workforce capable of delivering high‑quality, patient‑centered care.

answer_as_filed:
Wyandot Memorial Hospital participates in the 340B Drug Pricing Program as a critical access hospital to support its mission of providing accessible, high-quality care to all patients, regardless of ability to pay. Savings generated through the program are reinvested into patient care, service line support, workforce development, and community health initiatives that directly benefit the population served.
While the organization does not maintain a fully itemized accounting of each dollar of 340B program profit by individual expenditure, it monitors program performance through aggregate financial reporting, including total acquisition costs, reimbursement, and estimated net program savings. These funds are incorporated into the hospital’s operating budget and strategically allocated to sustain and expand essential services.
Although specific dollar amounts are not allocated at the individual program level, the organization uses its budgeting, financial reporting, and leadership oversight processes to ensure that 340B savings are reinvested into patient care, access-related services, community health initiatives, workforce support, and other programs that benefit the patients and communities served.
340B program savings directly and indirectly support a variety of programs, services, and initiatives, including but not limited to:
•	Lab Screening Program – Provides accessible and discounted health screenings through community health fairs and walk-in services, supporting early detection, prevention, and population health management through the hospital’s voucher system. Support from 340B savings helps reduce financial barriers for individuals who may otherwise delay or avoid routine laboratory testing due to cost. These screenings allow patients and community members to identify potential health concerns earlier, connect with appropriate follow-up care, and take proactive steps to manage chronic conditions such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and other preventable or treatable health risks.
•	Patient Navigator Program – Offers individualized care coordination and assistance securing resources for medications, follow-up services, specialty care, transportation needs, financial assistance, and other support services that may impact a patient’s ability to access care. Support from 340B savings helps sustain this role by allowing the hospital to connect patients with available programs, reduce barriers related to cost or logistics, and provide guidance throughout the care process. This support is especially important for patients managing chronic conditions, complex treatment plans, or limited resources, as it helps improve continuity of care, medication adherence, and timely access to needed services.
•	Community Health Education – Supports a wide range of school-based and community-based education efforts designed to improve health literacy, promote prevention, and connect individuals with resources before health concerns become more serious. These efforts include community health fairs, disease-specific education such as diabetic and cardiac education, stroke education, CPR training, Babysitter Clinic, career day activities, support groups, and other outreach events that address identified community needs. Support from 340B savings helps the hospital offer these programs in accessible formats, often at low or no cost to participants, while extending education beyond the hospital walls and into the communities it serves. These initiatives strengthen prevention efforts, encourage early intervention, support chronic disease management, and help individuals and families make informed decisions about their health and wellness.
•	Charity Care Program – Ensures access to medically necessary healthcare services for low-income, uninsured, underinsured, and underserved patients who may not qualify for other assistance programs. Support from 340B savings helps the hospital continue providing care regardless of a patient’s ability to pay, reduces financial barriers that may prevent individuals from seeking timely treatment, and supports follow-up care, diagnostic services, medication access, and other resources needed to promote better health outcomes within the community.
•	Student Education and Workforce Development – Supports clinical training, student placement, mentorship, and education programs for pharmacy, nursing, and allied health students, including partnerships with regional colleges and international programs. Support from 340B savings helps the hospital invest in the development of future healthcare professionals by providing hands-on learning opportunities in a rural hospital setting. These experiences expose students to critical access hospital operations, interdisciplinary care, medication management, patient-centered service delivery, and the unique healthcare needs of rural communities. 
•	Population Health and Public Health Initiatives – Includes participation in community health needs assessments, opioid reduction efforts, public health campaigns, and prevention-based programs designed to improve overall community wellness. Support from 340B savings helps the hospital identify and respond to priority health needs within the community, particularly for rural, underserved, and at-risk populations. These efforts include initiatives focused on chronic disease prevention, behavioral health awareness, substance use prevention and recovery support, immunization and screening education, injury prevention, healthy lifestyle promotion, and coordination with local public health and community partners. In addition to these programmatic investments, 340B savings support staffing resources, care delivery infrastructure, and operational stability, ensuring continued access to essential healthcare services in a rural setting.
As a critical access hospital serving a rural population, these reinvestments are essential to maintaining access to care, addressing health disparities, and supporting services that would otherwise be financially unsustainable. The organization remains committed to using 340B program benefits in a manner that aligns with both federal program intent and the healthcare needs of the community.
Wyandot Memorial Hospital maintains appropriate oversight and compliance processes to ensure adherence to 340B program requirements and responsible stewardship of program resources, with a continued focus on improving patient access, affordability, and quality of care.

answer_as_filed:
Highland District Hospital utilizes savings generated through the 340B Drug Pricing Program to strengthen access to healthcare services and improve affordability for the patients and communities we serve.

As a rural Critical Access Hospital, 340B savings help offset the financial burden associated with caring for uninsured and underinsured patients, allowing Highland District Hospital to continue providing medically necessary services regardless of a patient's ability to pay.

Additionally, 340B program savings support the availability of specialty care services that would otherwise be difficult to sustain in a rural community. These resources help make services such as pulmonology, general surgery, neurology, oncology, and pain management available locally, reducing the need for patients to travel outside Highland County to receive specialty care. By supporting these service lines, the 340B program improves access to timely, high-quality care while strengthening the long-term financial sustainability of essential healthcare services within our community.

Highland District Hospital remains committed to using 340B program savings to expand access to care, reduce financial barriers for patients, and ensure that residents of Highland County have access to a broad range of healthcare services close to home.

answer_as_filed: Fulton County Health Center used the resources generated through the 340B Drug Pricing Program to support access to comprehensive healthcare services for its rural community. In 2025, FCHC incurred approximately $1.07 million in uncompensated care costs and generated approximately $1.086 million in estimated 340B savings. 340B resources, together with other hospital resources, helped FCHC absorb uncompensated care and reimbursement shortfalls, maintain essential services that are not financially self-sustaining, including obstetric services, and expand community health services such as cardiac catheterization capabilities. Resources also help offset the financial impact of providing medically necessary care to patients covered by government-sponsored health plans when reimbursement does not fully cover the cost of care. These uses support FCHC's mission to maintain local access to care, serve patients regardless of ability to pay, and provide comprehensive services responsive to the needs of its rural community.

answer_as_filed: Ohio Hills Health Services (OHHS) began in 1976 and today provides medical, dental and behavioral health care services to 9300 Ohioans from 9 eastern Ohio counties. OHHC currently operates six health center locations in four counties including two school-based health centers. The OHHS service area covers 4,000 square miles. OHHS also provides free and discounted lab and health screenings that facilitate access to care for individuals and families in medically underserved communities, regardless of insurance status or ability to pay. OHHS maintains its role as the national voice for Community Health Centers and believes that high-quality primary health care is essential in creating healthy communities. Ohio Hills Health Services is a non-profit health care operation organized by communities in Eastern Ohio to promote healthy lifestyles and to provide comprehensive treatment and preventive services for area residents. The primary focus is to provide prompt, courteous, and affordable health care that is responsive and sensitive to individual needs. Ohio Hills Health Services is founded on the philosophy that the delivery of health care to the entire community and all its subgroups, including the medically indigent segment, is possible and practicable in a framework which does not separate subsets from total population and offers treatment regardless of economic status, race, national, geographic, or religious background, or political philosophy.

In CY 2025 OHHS utilized its 340B savings of $182,137.84 to fund free and discounted healthcare provided to qualified patients via the HRSA-required Sliding Fee Discount Program and to cover the financial loss of the HRSA-required dental program.

Sliding Fee Discount Program: Ohio Hills Health Services provided $101,001.00 in free and discounted medical, dental and behavioral health services throughout its service area in CY 2025. Part of the 340B savings covered the cost of this free and discounted care.

Dental Program: In CY 2025 the OHHS dental program experienced a bottom-line financial loss of -$83,398.05. OHHS provided free and discounted dental care to almost 3000 patients across 4 dental sites. OHHS is one of only a few dental providers in Eastern Ohio who accept Ohio Medicaid. The remaining balance of the CY 2025 340B savings covered the dental program financial loss.

In CY 2025 the 340B savings did not cover the combined loss of the Sliding Fee Discount Program and the Dental Program as indicated above. OHHS also provides quarterly discounted lab screenings, free skin cancer screenings and women’s health screenings to all community members at all OHHS health center sites. The cost of these screenings was absorbed by OHHS and could not be covered by the 340B savings in CY 2025.

answer_as_filed:
The reinvestment of our 340B savings has improved our community health as demonstrated through our patient outcomes, which have been recognized among the best in the nation. Without the 340B Program, we would not be able to provide comprehensive, team-based, high-quality care to our rural community.
Every dollar saved through the 340B Program is reinvested directly into patient care, allowing us to expand access to essential healthcare services, reduce barriers to treatment, and improve health outcomes for patients regardless of their ability to pay. These savings enable us to recruit and retain a multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals, invest in innovative care models, and offer services that would otherwise be financially unsustainable in a rural setting.
Our patients benefit from receiving comprehensive, coordinated care under one roof, eliminating the need to travel long distances for specialty services and improving continuity of care. Through the reinvestment of 340B savings, we are able to provide:
•	Family Medicine
•	Pediatrics
•	Internal Medicine
•	Women's Care
•	Behavioral Health
•	Psychiatry 
•	Dental Care
•	Diabetes Management and Education Classes
•	Eyecare
•	Pharmacy Retail Services
•	Clinical Pharmacy Services
•	Specialty Pharmacy
•	Registered Dietitian Services
•	Medication-Assisted Treatment
•	HIV and Hepatitis C Treatment
•	Hypertension Clinic
•	Wound Care
•	Adult Comprehensive Care
•	Specialty Care
•	Telemedicine
•	WIC (Women, Infants & Children)
•	Additional Patient Support Services
For many of our patients, these services represent the only accessible source of comprehensive healthcare within their community. The ability to integrate primary care, specialty care, pharmacy services, behavioral health, dental care, and other essential services creates a patient-centered medical home that improves chronic disease management, increases preventive care, reduces hospitalizations, and ultimately leads to healthier individuals and stronger communities.
The 340B Program is not simply a prescription drug discount program—it is a vital investment in rural healthcare infrastructure. It allows us to meet the unique needs of our community by expanding services, supporting vulnerable populations, and ensuring patients receive timely, coordinated, and affordable care close to home.

answer_as_filed:
Overview

NFP is a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) and part of the Health Resources and Services Administration’s (HRSA) Bureau of Primary Health Care Health Center Program. NFP has seven (7) registered associated sites located in the cities of Cleveland and Lakewood, Ohio. NFP provides integrated primary care, behavioral health, midwifery and breastfeeding, dental, refugee health, pharmacy, HIV prevention and treatment including Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program (RWHAP) Part A and Part C, and specialty services to people of all ages, regardless of their ability to pay. Last year, 72% of our 23,450 patients had incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty level.

NFP began participation in the 340B Program in 2000. Our 340B ID is CH050920. NFP has mechanisms in place to reasonably ensure compliance with all 340B program requirements, including mechanisms to prevent diversion and duplicate discount. NFP uses its 340B savings to stretch scarce Federal resources to help assist with many services such as interpretation, transportation, financial assistance, medication adherence assistance, patient education programs, pharmacy delivery services, food as medicine program and staff education.

340B Universe Program Details

Provider Administered Drugs (PADs)

Inclusive of the following associated site(s): Ridge Community Health Center (CHC), Tremont CHC, Ann B Reichsman CHC, Detroit Shoreway CHC, Puritas CHC, W 130th CHC, and North Coast CHC.

NFP has mechanisms in place to ensure 340B purchased drugs are utilized on qualifying patients by use of a physical inventory system. Administrations are documented in the electronic health record (EHR), EPIC OCHIN, from which patient specific auditable records are produced. NFP maintains both 340B and non-340B purchased drugs as inventory at the clinic(s). Primary purchasing accounts are established with the wholesaler(s) McKesson.

NFP has elected to carve-in Medicaid. Therefore, all National Provider Identifiers (NPIs) and 

Medicaid Provider Numbers (MPNs) used to bill Medicaid are listed on OPAIS and subsequently, the Medicaid Exclusion File (MEF). NFP monitors each state to which it bills Medicaid regularly to ensure compliance with state requirements to prevent duplicate discounts. State requirements to prevent duplicate discounts are met by including modifiers TB or SE on the prescription claims to identify them.

Entity Owned Retail Pharmacy

NFP operates three entity owned pharmacies at 3569 Ridge Road Cleveland, Ohio, 44102; 14625 Puritas Avenue Cleveland, Ohio, 44135; and 13027 Lorain Avenue Cleveland, Ohio, 44111. The pharmacies are open-door. The pharmacies utilize PioneerRx to process prescriptions. The pharmacies maintain a physical inventory system. Drug purchases are through McKesson. The in-house pharmacies have elected to carve-in Medicaid. Duplicate discounts are prevented by including the pharmacies NPIs on OPAIS and subsequently the MEF. State requirements to prevent duplicate discount are met by including modifiers 08 and 20 on the prescription claims to identify them.

Contract Pharmacy
 
NFP has Pharmacy Service Agreements with 19 contracted pharmacies to provide medications on behalf of NFP. WellPartner, 340B Complete, and 340B Direct Plus  are utilized to process and adjudicate prescriptions for 340B eligible patients. Patient specific encounter data is obtained from EPIC OCHIN and is sent to Wellpartner and 340B Direct Plus weekly and 340B Complete daily. An eligible provider list is updated at least quarterly.  All contract pharmacies carve-out Medicaid. A list of Medicaid payers for exclusion is updated regularly.

Program Monitoring 

Self-audits are completed regularly as outlined in NFP 340B Policies and Procedures to ensure program integrity and oversight. Any concerns are investigated and addressed according to policy and procedure.  Results of the self-audits are reviewed and discussed during 340B Oversight Team meetings. Independent external audits are performed annually.

answer_as_filed:
Health Partners of Western Ohio takes seriously its responsibility to use 340B savings to benefit patients and strengthen access to care in the communities we serve. These savings help bridge medication access gaps for uninsured patients, underinsured patients, and patients facing financial hardship.

As a safety net provider, HPWO also uses 340B savings to expand the range and reach of services available to our patients. Since opening our first pharmacy in 2006, HPWO has grown to include 25 additional sites, including locations in both urban and rural communities, 8 pharmacies, and 13 school-based health centers, and 8 dental operatories. All of which include behavioral health and substance abuse services . HPWO is also currently working on 4 separate building projects that will expand access to these services for even more patients.

Within our pharmacies, 340B savings have helped support adherence packaging services for patients across all 9 of our community health centers. More than 200 patients now receive this additional level of pharmacy support, which would not be possible at the same scale without 340B savings. HPWO plans to expand this service to eventually reach 1,000 patients.

340B savings also allow HPWO to offer free medication delivery 5 days per week at all pharmacy locations. This service is especially important as many of our communities have become pharmacy deserts due to widespread retail-chain pharmacy closures.

Overall, 340B savings allow HPWO to continue growing, serving more patients, expanding needed services, and improving the quality of care we provide. Most importantly, these savings help ensure that individual patients can access needed medications without financial barriers.

340B Community Impact Report:
Famiily Medical Centers
Ironton-Lawrence County Area CAO, Inc.
Serving our Community Through the 340B Drug Pricing Program

Our Mission and Community:   Family Medical Centers, a program of Ironton-Lawrence County CAO, Inc., is committed to providing high-quality, patient-centered care to individuals and families across our service area.  We serve patients regardless of their ability to pay, focusing on those who are uninsured, underinsured, and medically underserved.
The 340B Drug Pricing Program allows our organization to stretch limited resources and expand access to essential services for our community.

What the 340B Program Means to Our Health Center:  Through the 340B program, Family Medical Centers can purchase medications at reduced prices. The savings generated are not retained as profit.  Instead, they are reinvested directly into patient care and community services to fulfill our mission and meet the needs of our patients.

How 340B Savings Support Our Patients:  
Access to Medications:  340B savings help reduce medication costs for patients, including those on a sliding fee scale, improving affordability and adherence.
Expanded Services:  Savings are reinvested to support primary care, behavioral health, dental services, and chronic disease management programs.
Addressing Barriers to Care: Funds support enabling services such as transportation assistance, care coordination, and translation services, ensuring patients can access the care they need.
Sustaining Care for Vulnerable Populations: 340B savings help offset uncompensated care and allow the health center to continue serving patients regardless of ability to pay.

Impact on Our Community:
340B savings enable Family Medical Centers to serve more patients, expand services, and improve helath outcomes in our community.  These investments allow us to deliver comprehensive, whole-person care and respond to emerging community health needs.

Why 340B Matters:
Without the 340B program, our ability to provide affordable medications and essential services would be significantly reduced.  With 340B, we are able to expand access to care, improve health outcomes, and strengthen the overall health of the community we serve.

Looking Ahead: Family Medical Centers remains committed to leveraging 340B savings to enhance services, improve patient outcomes, and address the evolving needs of our community.  We continue to invest in programs that promote health equity and access to care.

answer_as_filed:
The 340B Drug Pricing Program plays an important role in supporting Care Alliance Health Center's clinical operations and financial sustainability. Savings generated through the program are reinvested to support patient care, pharmacy operations, clinical staffing, care coordination, community outreach, and other organizational functions that improve access to comprehensive healthcare services for medically underserved populations.

Care Alliance provides integrated primary care, behavioral health, pharmacy, women's health, infectious disease, and substance use disorder services across multiple clinical and community-based settings. The organization serves patients residing in public housing, individuals receiving substance use treatment, people experiencing homelessness through men's and women's shelters, school-based populations, and other underserved communities throughout Northeast Ohio. 340B savings help offset the cost of providing care to uninsured and underinsured patients while supporting access to high-cost medications for HIV treatment and prevention, opioid use disorder, women's health, and other chronic conditions.

As the healthcare landscape continues to evolve, Care Alliance anticipates an increased reliance on 340B program savings to help maintain organizational stability and preserve access to care. Medicaid work requirements and other policy changes may increase the number of patients experiencing interruptions in insurance coverage or financial barriers to obtaining medications. Continued reinvestment of 340B savings allows the organization to sustain essential clinical services, maintain operational capacity, and ensure vulnerable populations continue to receive coordinated, high-quality care regardless of their ability to pay.

answer_as_filed:
Heart of Ohio Family Health Centers operates six clinical sites across four Central Ohio zip codes, serving more than 21,000 patients through over 100,000 encounters annually. Our patient population carries a disproportionately high social determinants of health burden, including a significant volume of high-risk pregnancies and individuals for whom Heart of Ohio Family Health is the only consistent source of primary care. 

Retail pharmacy operations generated 43% of the organization's gross revenue in FY2025. The 340B program functions as operational infrastructure, not a discrete initiative. 340B savings are absorbed into the daily cost of delivering care across primary care, dental, behavioral health, prenatal and pharmacy services. Without 340B, entire service lines would be financially unviable and thousands of patients would lose access to care. 

The 340B program has reduced our reliance on federal and state grant funding to less than 7% of our total operating budget. This stability translates directly to outcomes: Heart of Ohio Family Health has received multiple HRSA Quality awards as well as national recognition from the American Heart Association for positive clinical outcomes achieved with a patient population facing substancial barriers to care.

answer_as_filed: 340B Savings are used for expanding Patient Services, Improving Access to Care, Strengthening Operations.  At Valley View Health Centers, a division of Community Action Committee of Pike County, we treat all who come to us regardless of their ability to pay. We provide care to patients who live in an area hit hard with the opioid epidemic and poverty. We strive to address social determinants of health by providing access to care, education, housing, transportation, food security, etc. The 340B Drug Discount Program is a federal government program created in 1992 that requires drug manufacturers to provide outpatient drugs to eligible health care organizations and covered entities to stretch scarce federal resources as far as possible, reaching more eligible patients and providing more comprehensive services. We invest in new facilities and equipment to make accessing health care services easier and provide the best in technology and services. We widen our service area through school-based expansion, offer telehealth and remote services to remove geographical barriers. We expand care options by expanding case management services all at locations. We fight food insecurities through a mobile food pantry, increased case management to assist with housing, transportation, etc. We remove barriers by utilize technology to provide access to care using telehealth to reach our most rural patients who may struggle with transportation. We strive to improve insurance verification and authorization process, appointment scheduling and registration, and work to address the shortage of providers. We strive to improve communication, standardized processes, workflows, and leadership that serves to achieve better outcomes for our patients. We work with community partners to build strong relationships that better serve our patients. We strengthen cash on hand to ensure we don’t experience cash shortages that could negatively impact patient access.

MVHC operates twelve (12) locations within a four-county
region including Muskingum, Morgan, Guernsey, and Coshocton counties. MVHC serves over 73,000
patients annually, resulting in over 282,000 visits. MVHC offers services including primary care services,
women’s health, dental health, podiatry, behavioral health, and addiction services. Additionally, MVHC
operates two in-house pharmacies and one specialty pharmacy in Muskingum and Guernsey counties.  Our medical and pharmacy services are available to low-income patients on the sliding-fee scale, and we serve all patients regardless of their insurance.  In addition to providing free transportation to our patients, and offering Mobile Health services, we also provide free prescription deliver- impacting patients with transportation barriers to accessing healthcare.

label_as_filed: (Narrative) Provide additional detail/context as necessary:
answer_as_filed: 2025 was our first full year of having our own pharmacies. Given the unknowns, the salaries of $387K for pharmacists and the $130K for our clinical pharmacists were sustained using H80 Grant funds. We had additional $8K in audit/consulting work done, which was not billed until 2026. This year we are transitioning the full costs of our pharmacy to the 340B program. We anticipate that the surplus funds will be used to remodel the building we purchased in early 2026 and to finance the mortgage on the building. We are increasing our foot print in Alliance, OH and hope to offer expanded services with the addition of dentistry, a very needed service in this community. We have already expanded our clinical pharmacy program in 2026 and have also hired an Engagement Pharmacist to improve our capture rate and the communication between our patients and pharmacy services & staff.

answer_as_filed: The HealthCare Connection utilizes savings generated through the 340B Drug Pricing Program to expand access to comprehensive healthcare services for underserved and vulnerable populations in our community. Rather than distributing these funds as profit, 340B savings are reinvested into programs and services that support our mission as a Federally Qualified Health Center.

Specifically, 340B savings help offset the cost of providing care to uninsured and underinsured patients, support expanded pharmacy services, maintain medication access programs, and fund clinical staff and care coordination services that are not fully reimbursed by third-party payers. These funds also help sustain behavioral health, dental, vision, and primary care services, improve patient access through extended hours and care management, and support investments in technology, equipment, and infrastructure that enhance patient care.

As reimbursement rates often do not fully cover the cost of providing comprehensive healthcare services, 340B savings are essential to maintaining financial sustainability while allowing The HealthCare Connection to continue expanding services, improving health outcomes, and reducing barriers to care for the communities we serve.

answer_as_filed: During calendar year 2025, Lorain County Health & Dentistry (LCH&D) provided approximately 4,100 patient encounters for 2,047 uninsured patients. In accordance with our Board-approved Sliding Fee Discount Program and HRSA requirements, LCH&D adjusted $978,583.33 in patient fees for these uninsured encounters. These adjustments represent the difference between the full charges for services provided and the reduced amounts patients were responsible for paying based on their eligibility under the Sliding Fee Discount Program. A total of $420,531.47 in 340B program savings was used to offset a portion of these discounted services, helping ensure uninsured patients continued to receive access to comprehensive medical, behavioral health, dental, OB/GYN, and vision services regardless of their ability to pay. The remaining cost of these fee adjustments was supported through other organizational resources.

answer_as_filed:
Lorain County Health & Dentistry (LCH&D), a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC), is committed to serving the underserved and uninsured residents of Lorain County by providing comprehensive, high-quality healthcare regardless of a patient's ability to pay. Our integrated services include primary medical care, behavioral health, dental care, obstetrics and gynecology (OB/GYN), and vision services. The 340B Drug Pricing Program plays a vital role in supporting our mission by allowing us to stretch limited resources and reinvest savings into patient care and expanded access to services. In 2025, we expanded our pharmacy services by opening a second in-house pharmacy, improving access to affordable medications for our patients. We also provide a mail-order pharmacy service to ensure patients who face transportation or other barriers can conveniently receive their medications. During 2025, LCH&D served 17,588 unique patients through 58,005 patient visits. Of those, 2,047 patients were uninsured and accounted for approximately 4,100 patient encounters. These uninsured patients were offered services under our Sliding Fee Discount Program based on their household income and ability to pay. Savings generated through the 340B Program helped offset the cost of providing care to these patients, allowing us to continue delivering essential healthcare services while maintaining financial sustainability. It is also important to note that a portion of the prescriptions reported as "cash" sales reflects situations where patients elected to purchase medications at our discounted cash price because it was less expensive than using their insurance benefits. This commonly occurs when a patient's insurance deductible or out-of-pocket cost is significantly higher than our pharmacy's cash price (for example, a $250 copayment or deductible). These transactions are recorded as cash sales, making them difficult to separately quantify, but they represent an important way the 340B Program helps reduce medication costs for our patients.

LCH&D does not administer 340B-purchased drugs. All medications administered within our clinics are non-340B drugs.

Primary Care - Additional staff, offsetting underpayments, equipment, etc: The Centers provides comprehensive primary care for the entire family — from routine check-ups and preventive care to sick visits and ongoing support for chronic health conditions. Primary care services include:
•	Routine check-ups and well visits
•	Sick and urgent care visits
•	Vaccines and flu shots
•	Chronic care management
•	Pediatric care

answer_as_filed: Schizophrenia Specialized Treatment, Advocacy, and Recovery Services: This specialized program is designed to provide comprehensive, coordinated and evidence-based care for individuals experiencing schizophrenia spectrum disorders. answer_as_filed: School Based Therapy for Children: SB-BHT provides individual counseling to youth in charter and public schools throughout Cuyahoga County. answer_as_filed: Pharmacy expense coverage - Staff, Clinical Pharmacists, etc: At The Centers, the pharmacy is a part of our patients’ healthcare team. We provide low-cost prescriptions, convenient locations, fast prescription refills and affordable options with a sliding fee scale, payment plans and more. We also now have free home delivery to reduce barriers and increase accessibility. Our team of clinical pharmacists co-manage medication treatment plans for patients with chronic diseases alongside providers. They also manage clinical monitoring programs as well as compliance packaging.

answer_as_filed: The Centers reinvests 100 percent of its 340B program savings to expand access to high-quality, comprehensive health care and supportive services for underserved patients throughout our community. Consistent with the intent of Congress, 340B savings strengthen our ability to provide care regardless of a patient's ability to pay and help offset significant reimbursement shortfalls in behavioral health, primary care, dental care, pharmacy, and other essential services. These funds support critical clinical staff, care coordination, pharmacy operations, specialized treatment programs, school-based services for children, and innovative crisis and recovery services that would otherwise be difficult or impossible to sustain. By reinvesting 340B savings directly into patient care and community health initiatives, The Centers is able to serve more patients, enhance care quality, address social determinants of health, and meet growing community needs while maintaining access to services that are vital to the health and well-being of the populations we serve.

answer_as_filed:
The 340B Program enables safety-net providers like FRHC to stretch limited federal resources, ensuring that underserved patients receive affordable medications and comprehensive care. Compliance with federal 340B requirements ensures that savings are used solely to benefit our patients and expand access to essential services.

 FRHC reinvests 340B savings to offset medication costs and reduce out-of-pocket expenses for eligible patients, support critical service lines that operate at a loss, including Obstetrics/Gynecology and Dental, expand specialty services such as Vision, Podiatry, Sports Medicine, and Infectious Disease, and develop and sustain additional service locations to meet patient needs across our multi-county region.

 Without the 340B Program, FRHC would be unable to maintain the depth and breadth of services currently available to our patients. The program’s impact is integral to our ability to fulfill our mission and meet the needs of our community.

answer_as_filed:
Centerpoint Health provides a comprehensive system of care that extends beyond traditional medical services and is not fully funded through patient service revenue or Section 330 grant funding. These services are essential to addressing barriers to care, improving health outcomes, and supporting Centerpoint Health’s mission of serving medically underserved populations throughout Southwest Ohio.
Many patients experience barriers that extend beyond clinical needs, including language access challenges, transportation limitations, low health literacy, socioeconomic instability, and difficulty navigating the healthcare system. To address these needs, Centerpoint Health provides enabling services that improve access to and engagement in care.
These services include medical interpretation and translation for patients with limited English proficiency, patient navigation to support access to community resources.  Additional services include care coordination and case management services for individuals with chronic conditions, behavioral health needs, and complex social circumstances, and nutrition services that support chronic disease management, preventive care, and patient education.
Centerpoint Health also invests in quality improvement and population health activities, including clinical quality monitoring, care gap outreach, preventive care initiatives, value-based care support, regulatory compliance, and implementation of evidence-based interventions. While essential to improving outcomes, these activities are generally not separately reimbursed through patient service revenue.
Additional support services are provided to address social determinants of health, including outreach, eligibility assistance, and community resource referrals. These services improve health outcomes and reduce disparities but often require funding beyond traditional reimbursement sources.
A significant portion of resources is also directed toward uncompensated care, including services provided to uninsured and underinsured patients, sliding fee scale discounts, discounted or unreimbursed prescription drugs, and costs not fully covered due to payer limitations, coverage gaps, or reimbursement rates that do not reflect the full cost of care. These costs reflect essential services delivered in alignment with Centerpoint Health’s mission and commitment to access to care.
As a result, the cost of delivering comprehensive, patient-centered care exceeds what is covered through net patient revenue and Section 330 funding alone. Additional funding sources are necessary to sustain these critical services and ensure continued access to high-quality, affordable care for the communities Centerpoint Health serves.

answer_as_filed: The health center does not maintain a separate accounting system that tracks individual expenditures tied directly to 340B savings.  Revenue generated through the 340B program is deposited into the organization's general operating funds and is used to support the overall mission of the Federally Qualified Health Center.   Consistent with applicable federal requirements, 340B program savings are used to expand and sustain access to comprehensive healthcare services for our patient population.  Rather than being assigned to specific purchases or programs, these funds help offset the operating costs of clinical services that are not fully supported through patient reimbursement alone.  340B savings contribute to the financial sustainability of the organization by supporting expenses including, but not limited to: primary care services, behavioral health services, dental services, care coordination and other patient support services, personnel salaries and benefits, medical and operational supplies, other allowable operating expenses necesssary to provide comprehensive healthcare services.  Because these funds are commingled with other operating revenues within the health center's general operating budget, the organization cannot provide a detailed accounting of specific expenditures that were funded exclusively with 340B savings.  Instead, 340B program savings strengthen the overall financial capacity of the health center, allowing it to maintain and expand services for medically underserved patients, support programs that operate at a financial loss, and fulfill its mission of providing accessible, comprehensive healthcare regardless of a patient's ability to pay.

answer_as_filed:
This surplus has been used to support the other FQHC services provided by SpringVale to qualified patients.  These dollars cover gaps in expenses not covered by service income generated or HRSA grant dollar in:
Primary Care
Rapid Care Medical (including radiology)
OBGYN
Dental Services 
Behavioral Health Services

The biggest reallocation of income from the pharmacy is in Rapid Care Medical and Dental Services.  These programs are vital to supporting our community but fall short of covering the 2025 cost of these services.  Pharmacy surplus has closed that gap in these services and the others listed above.

Pharmacy surplus also helped cover start up cost in opening our new location at Oxford Street.  This new location in providing the existing services and now Psych Med Management services under our FQHC certification.  These are all services that would not be successful as they are without the pharmacy surplus we are grateful for.

Compass Community Health (CCH) uses the financial benefit generated through its participation in the 340B Drug Pricing Program to support and expand access to comprehensive, affordable healthcare for the patients and communities it serves. These savings allow CCH to stretch limited resources, offset the cost of caring for uninsured and underinsured patients, support the Sliding Fee Discount Program, and sustain services for which reimbursement may not cover the full cost of care.
The 340B savings also contribute to the continued operation of Compass Pharmacy and CCH’s efforts to improve access to affordable medications and promote medication adherence. In addition, these resources help support primary care, women’s health, mental health, pediatric occupational and speech therapy, care coordination, outreach, patient education, clinical staffing, technology, supplies, and other services necessary to meet identified community needs.
By reinvesting the benefit of the 340B Program into health center operations and patient services, CCH reduces financial and access barriers, maintains and expands essential services, and provides more comprehensive care to medically underserved individuals.

answer_as_filed:
Highland Health Providers (HHP) uses revenue generated through the 340B Drug Pricing Program to expand access to care, improve patient outcomes, and reduce financial barriers for the medically underserved patients we serve. The program has allowed HHP to reinvest savings directly into services that would not otherwise be financially sustainable in our rural community.
340B revenue has also enabled HHP to expand clinical services that improve chronic disease management and preventive care. These investments include:
•	Providing registered dietitian nutrition services and diabetes education at no cost to patients, improving self-management of chronic conditions and reducing barriers to education.
•	Adding a dedicated Clinical Care Coordinator to assist patients in navigating complex healthcare needs, coordinating specialty referrals, and improving continuity of care.
•	Hiring two Prior Authorization Specialists to help patients obtain timely approval for medically necessary medications and treatments, reducing delays in care.
•	Employing a Quality Improvement Specialist focused on population health management, preventive screenings, and quality initiatives that improve patient outcomes.
HHP also invested in the implementation of the Epic electronic health record (EHR) system. This significant infrastructure investment improves care coordination across healthcare settings by allowing providers to more effectively exchange health information with hospitals, specialists, and tertiary care centers. As a result, patients experience smoother transitions of care, improved communication among providers, and enhanced continuity of treatment.
Additionally, HHP's entity-owned pharmacy operates a 340B Supplemental Discount Program that provides additional copay assistance to eligible patients. Under this program, patients facing high out-of-pocket medication costs may receive prescriptions at a standardized discounted price based on insurance remits, deductibles, and medication acquisition costs. This supplemental assistance helps ensure that cost does not become a barrier to medication adherence.
Collectively, these investments demonstrate HHP's commitment to reinvesting 340B program savings into expanded access, enhanced clinical services, improved care coordination, health information technology, and direct financial assistance for patients. The 340B program has allowed HHP to strengthen the healthcare safety net while improving the quality, affordability, and accessibility of care for the rural communities we serve.

answer_as_filed:
OSU Total Health Care Center (THCC) utilizes 340B program savings and revenue in direct support of its mission to serve underserved and vulnerable patient populations in two primary ways. 

First, program savings are applied to assist patients experiencing financial hardship in accessing prescribed medications they would otherwise be unable to afford, consistent with the health center's Sliding Fee Discount Program. 

Second, program revenue supports the salaries and fringe benefits of clinical and patient support personnel whose roles directly advance care access and quality, including clinical pharmacy staff, Community Health Workers, and care coordinators. 

All 340B funds are reinvested into health center operations consistent with HRSA requirements and 340B program integrity guidelines.

answer_as_filed: Southern Ohio Medical Center (SOMC) is located in Portsmouth, Ohio and is a private nonprofit with a contract with the government. SOMC has forty-six (46) registered child sites serving patients in Southern Ohio and North-Eastern Kentucky. SOMC has been listed as a 340B covered entity since April 1, 2005. SOMC uses its 340B savings to stretch scarce Federal resources to reduce the cost of drugs to vulnerable patients and expand access to care by establishing primary care & selected specialty care services in under-served areas with significant indigent populations. SOMC's Specialty Pharmacy runs a patient-centered Chronic Disease Management program for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma, hypercholesterolemia, atrial fibrillation, and congestive heart failure (CHF). SOMC has a Discharge Pharmacy near the Emergency Department (ED) with extended hours. This allows patients to pick up prescriptions before leaving the hospital and improves medication adherence. SOMC's "Meds to Beds" program enables patients to receive prescription education and medications at their bedside upon discharge. Financial assistance is provided to patients that can't afford their medication. SOMC has 8 open door retail pharmacies and has plans to continue to expand its retail pharmacy footprint in an effort to reach even more vulnerable patients in remote areas. The organization also operates an infusion center, an anticoagulation clinic, and an anti-arrhythmia clinic.  These services would not be viable without the 340B Program.

answer_as_filed: In calendar year 2025, Mount Carmel St. Ann's retained approximately $2,973,314 in savings under the 340B Drug Pricing Program, measured as the difference between the GPO price and the actual 340B or WAC acquisition price for each purchase (per Macro Helix's net savings report). These savings are reinvested into Mount Carmel's charitable mission and Community Health & Well-Being programs, which extend care beyond the hospital to underserved and vulnerable central Ohio residents, including the programs listed above. The cost of these community programs exceeds the 340B savings retained. System-wide in fiscal year 2025 (July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025), Mount Carmel provided more than $136.1 million in IRS-defined community benefit as part of $282.5 million in total community impact.

label_as_filed: If Covered Entity cannot provide a detailed accounting as requested above, provide a detailed narrative regarding how 340B funds/profits are used.
answer_as_filed: Mount Carmel does not maintain 340B program savings in separate, program-specific accounts. The savings shown represent the covered entity's total 340B savings for the reporting period (GPO-price basis); these funds are reinvested into the covered entity's overall charitable mission and community benefit rather than tracked as discrete per-program 340B expenditures. Accordingly, an exact dollar-by-dollar accounting of 340B savings by individual program is not available. The programs identified above, the total savings figure, and the covered entity's documented community benefit together represent its good-faith accounting of how 340B savings are used.
