answer_as_filed: Savings realized through Summa Health's participation in the 340B Drug Pricing Program helped preserve and strengthen services that were important to the health of the communities we served. These resources provided additional financial capacity to care for patients who may have had difficulty obtaining needed healthcare because of limited income, inadequate insurance coverage, or other medical and social challenges. The benefit of the 340B program extended beyond medication costs. Savings helped Summa sustain services such as our Complex Care Clinic, Senior Health Clinic, and behavioral health programs, including psychiatric and addiction services. These programs provided important access points for patients whose healthcare needs required ongoing clinical management, coordination among multiple providers, or additional support outside of a traditional office visit.Summa also worked to identify and address non-medical circumstances that could interfere with a patient's ability to successfully receive care. Community outreach and patient support efforts helped address needs such as transportation, access to medications, coordination of healthcare services, and connections to appropriate social resources. Addressing these challenges helped patients remain engaged in their treatment, take medications as prescribed, and receive appropriate care earlier in the course of an illness. The financial resources made available through 340B also supported Summa's ability to provide charity care, medication assistance, and free or reduced-cost services to patients who otherwise may have had difficulty accessing them. These efforts were particularly important for uninsured and underinsured individuals and others facing significant barriers to healthcare. Ultimately, the 340B program helped Summa direct healthcare resources toward areas of significant community need. The savings generated through the program strengthened our ability to maintain essential services, support vulnerable patient populations, and improve access to coordinated care. This reinvestment supported Summa's broader mission of improving the health of the communities we served while helping reduce disparities in access to healthcare and treatment.

(Narrative) Provide additional detail/context as necessary:
answer_as_filed: From January 1 through December 2, 2025 (DSH360035 Eligible Program Participation), Mount Carmel East and Grove City retained approximately $7,045,615 in savings under the 340B Drug Pricing Program, measured as the difference between the GPO price and the actual 340B or WAC acquisition price for each purchase (per Macro Helix's net savings report). These savings are reinvested into Mount Carmel's charitable mission and Community Health & Well-Being programs, which extend care beyond the hospital to underserved and vulnerable central Ohio residents, including the programs listed above. The cost of these community programs exceeds the 340B savings retained. System-wide in fiscal year 2025 (July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025), Mount Carmel provided more than $136.1 million in IRS-defined community benefit as part of $282.5 million in total community impact.

answer_as_filed: The information presented above provides an overview of the programs and services that are made possible, in part, through savings generated by the 340B Drug Pricing Program. For The University of Toledo Medical Center (UTMC), the 340B Program is not a discrete revenue source or a stand-alone funding mechanism. Rather, it is an integral component of the organization's financial structure that helps sustain access to care for Medicaid beneficiaries, uninsured individuals, and other medically complex and underserved patients.In fiscal year 2025, UToledo Health reported an operating income of approximately $5.4 million. The savings generated through the 340B Program play a critical role in supporting this financial stability and are reinvested to maintain essential clinical services, expand access to care, and offset the significant costs associated with caring for a high proportion of government-insured and uninsured patients. answer_as_filed: Miami Valley Hospital and Atrium Medical Center qualify for the 340B program and collectively saved $69.9 million and $54.0 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively. 340B savings assist health systems in partially subsidizing services to patients that operate at a loss. Consistent with Premier Health’s mission, care is provided to patients regardless of the patient’s ability to pay. For patients who qualify as charity care based on their inability to pay, the estimated cost incurred by Premier Health to provide these services, less recognized charity care subsidies, was $31.4 million and $22.7 million for 2025 and 2024 respectively. Also consistent with Premier Health’s mission, services are provided to Medicare and Medicaid covered patients where payment is not sufficient to cover the cost of providing the service. The shortfall of payment to cost in unreimbursed Medicaid, Medicare and other means-tested government programs totaled $395.0 million and $449.8 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively. Premier Health also provided other community health improvement, community benefit and subsidized health services totaling $45.3 million and $86.1 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively. The savings from the 340B program play a critical role in ensuring access to many health services to patients regardless of their ability to pay, and the savings only cover a small portion of the overall unfunded and underfunded care provided across all patients.

answer_as_filed:
How 340B Savings Support MetroHealth Patients:
 
The MetroHealth System is Cuyahoga County's public safety-net health system, caring for more than 300,000 patients regardless of their ability to pay. MetroHealth participates in the 340B Program with services provided through two types of covered entities: MetroHealth Medical Center, a disproportionate share hospital (DSH), and MetroHealth Community Health Centers, a federally qualified health center (FQHC). The benefits described below reflect the coordinated work of both covered entities to provide comprehensive patient care services to the region. Public hospitals and Community Health Centers like ours care for the community's most medically and socially vulnerable, low-income residents. They are exactly the providers Congress intended to benefit when it created the 340B Program. MetroHealth Medical Center was the second hospital in Ohio to join the program, in early 1994.
 
Our patients face barriers to health that extend well beyond the exam room: 22% experience housing instability, 22% face food insecurity, 13% deal with transportation insecurity, and 17.5% live below the federal poverty level. More than two-thirds rely on government insurance programs like Medicaid or Medicare, or are uninsured.
 
340B savings allow MetroHealth to stretch limited resources further and reinvest them in care and services that would otherwise be reduced or unavailable. Most importantly, the program lets us bring life-saving medications and outpatient care to the neighborhoods where our patients live. That keeps people out of the emergency department and lowers the risk that their conditions become life-threatening. Because of 340B, MetroHealth is:
 
• Making medications affordable: MetroHealth offers four levels of financial assistance for Cuyahoga County residents with incomes up to 400% of the federal poverty level. These plans provide comprehensive care, including prescription drugs, at no cost or at a steeply discounted cost. Patients who don't qualify can receive vouchers and copay assistance to lower what they pay at the pharmacy. Our financial assistance coordinators also help any patient find lower-cost medications, manufacturer assistance and other programs. They also help patients get specialty drugs for cancer, HIV, hepatitis C, rheumatologic and cardiovascular conditions at affordable prices. Last year, that work saved patients more than $52 million. And because our pharmacy prices average 25–30% below other retail pharmacies, we lower costs for payers as well.
 
• Getting patients on treatment faster: For specialty and high-cost medications, insurance approvals are often what delays care. MetroHealth's Specialty Pharmacy and centralized prior authorization call center take that work on. They handle insurer requirements, secure approvals and find financial assistance. In 2025, the team completed 54,250 prior authorizations with an average turnaround of about 18 hours. Patients start therapy sooner and stay on it, and our providers can spend their time treating patients instead of doing paperwork.
 
• Bringing care into the neighborhoods: Our more than 20 outpatient locations across Cleveland and Cuyahoga County offer primary and specialty care, dental, vision and behavioral health services for all ages. Patients who qualify receive this care free or at significantly reduced cost. These sites keep people healthy and out of the hospital, but the network runs at a significant financial loss, which 340B savings help offset.
 
• Expanding pharmacy access: MetroHealth operates twelve community retail pharmacies in neighborhoods where our patients live, including areas that became pharmacy deserts when chain pharmacies closed. These locations offer free vaccinations and no-cost home delivery. At our main campus, a 24/7 pharmacy with drive-through service is open to anyone in the community who needs medication after an Emergency Department visit, after hours, or when other pharmacies are closed.
 
• Putting pharmacists on the care team: MetroHealth embeds pharmacists in clinical areas as part of our inpatient and ambulatory care teams. There they work directly with patients and adjust treatment as needs change, improving health outcomes.
 
• Sending patients home with their medications: Our bedside delivery program brings prescriptions to patients before discharge, so they don't need an extra trip to the pharmacy. No-cost home delivery continues after they get home. For patients with transportation, mobility or other barriers, this makes it far more likely they start and stay on their medications. That helps prevent complications and avoidable return visits to the hospital. Delivery also supports our antimicrobial stewardship efforts. When culture results or clinical review show that a patient needs a different antibiotic after discharge, our pharmacy team coordinates the change and delivers the new antibiotic to the patient's home the same day.
 
• Supporting mothers, babies and families: MetroHealth partners with the community to improve maternal and infant health and reduce infant mortality. 340B savings have helped expand access to midwives and doulas, home visits through our Nurse-Family Partnership team, and CenteringPregnancy programs that support pregnant women early and often throughout pregnancy.
 
• Keeping care going through crises: 340B resources helped MetroHealth maintain access to medications and uninterrupted care through major disruptions. These included the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2024 Change Healthcare cyberattack, which disrupted pharmacy services nationwide.
 
• Caring for patients who have nowhere else to turn: In 2025, MetroHealth provided $358 million in charity care, nearly $1 million every day. 340B savings give a public safety-net system the financial flexibility to keep offering Level I trauma care, adult and pediatric burn care, primary and specialty care, and other essential services to everyone, regardless of ability to pay.
 
Without 340B savings, MetroHealth would have far fewer resources to sustain these services, and the impact would reach well beyond the pharmacy counter. Financial assistance, neighborhood clinics, pharmacy access and the programs that help patients overcome barriers to care would all come under pressure. For many of our patients, 340B is the difference between getting care close to home and getting care only in an emergency room.

answer_as_filed:
"Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B Drug Pricing Program to continue to provide the highest quality care for the communities we serve. By lowering the cost of eligible outpatient medications, 340B helps us redirect resources into patient care, pharmacy access and essential services for people who might otherwise have limited access to treatment. For Cleveland Clinic, 340B helps us stretch limited resources so we can continue serving as a safety net for highly specialized care, while also supporting patients experiencing unmet needs.
Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B benefit to help provide access to care, preserve access points and reinvest in broader community health efforts. In 2024 alone (the most recent year for which complete data are available), we provided $337.7 million in free or discounted care to more than 139,000 patients, contributed $1.49 billion in community benefit across Ohio, Florida and Nevada, and provided $28.7 million in subsidized health services that meet important community needs despite operating at a loss.
340B also helps Cleveland Clinic maintain pharmacy access and reduce barriers to medication adherence. Examples include operating 27 retail pharmacy locations across Northeast Ohio, opening a new community pharmacy at South Pointe Hospital in 2025, delivering, at no delivery cost, discharge prescriptions to patients and providing transition-of-care pharmacist support for patients after discharge.
For more information on how Cleveland Clinic uses 340B savings please visit our website at https://my.clevelandclinic.org/about/community/reports/340b-program
"

answer_as_filed:
Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B Drug Pricing Program to continue to provide the highest quality care for the communities we serve. By lowering the cost of eligible outpatient medications, 340B helps us redirect resources into patient care, pharmacy access and essential services for people who might otherwise have limited access to treatment. For Cleveland Clinic, 340B helps us stretch limited resources so we can continue serving as a safety net for highly specialized care, while also supporting patients experiencing unmet needs.
Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B benefit to help provide access to care, preserve access points and reinvest in broader community health efforts. In 2024 alone (the most recent year for which complete data are available), we provided $337.7 million in free or discounted care to more than 139,000 patients, contributed $1.49 billion in community benefit across Ohio, Florida and Nevada, and provided $28.7 million in subsidized health services that meet important community needs despite operating at a loss.
340B also helps Cleveland Clinic maintain pharmacy access and reduce barriers to medication adherence. Examples include operating 27 retail pharmacy locations across Northeast Ohio, opening a new community pharmacy at South Pointe Hospital in 2025, delivering, at no delivery cost, discharge prescriptions to patients and providing transition-of-care pharmacist support for patients after discharge.
For more information on how Cleveland Clinic uses 340B savings please visit our website at https://my.clevelandclinic.org/about/community/reports/340b-program

answer_as_filed:
The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center (“Ohio State”) is a public, academic health center that provides care to a high volume of Medicare and Medicaid patients. In 2024, around 71% of the patients served in our University Hospitals were covered by government programs or self-pay, including Medicare (34.6%) and Medicaid only (26.8%). Our service area is the entire state of Ohio, with more than 50% of our inpatient admissions being patients from Columbus and Franklin County, 16% coming from adjacent counties and 32% coming from other counties in Ohio outside of central Ohio.

Ohio State operates highly specialized health care programs that are essential to our community but are not always financially self-sustaining. Many of these services including our trauma, transplant, inpatient detoxification, outpatient behavioral health, and high-risk obstetrics programs care for a disproportionate share of patients who are uninsured or covered by Medicare and Medicaid.  Reimbursement of these services often falls short of the costs to provide care. 

Ohio State's Emergency Department operates around the clock as a regional trauma center, serving patients of all acuity levels, regardless of ability to pay. Federal law guarantees access to patients but does not guarantee adequate reimbursement for those providers. 340B savings help sustain the staffing and infrastructure needed to deliver that care safely.  

Other essential programs, such as Ohio State’s Labor & Delivery unit, receive high-risk referrals from hospitals across the region that lack the specialty capacity to safely manage complex pregnancies. Ohio State serves a significant share of Medicaid-covered mothers, and reimbursement consistently falls short of the costs of care. 340B savings help close that gap.

Ohio's behavioral health crisis is acute, and Ohio State is among the state's largest providers of inpatient and outpatient psychiatric care. Ohio State serves patients with severe mental illness, substance use disorders, and acute psychiatric crises.  Many of these patients are uninsured or covered by Medicaid at rates below the cost of care. 340B savings help sustain the staffing and services that keep these programs open and accessible.

Ohio State’s Medication Access Team ensures patients can obtain and afford the medications their providers prescribe. By removing insurance, financial, and administrative barriers, the team secures prior authorization approvals and connects patients to manufacturer assistance programs, grants, copay support, vouchers, and the Ohio State Medication Repository Program. Working directly with patients, providers, payers, and manufacturers, Medication Access Specialists navigate complex access requirements to prevent delays in treatment, reduce medication abandonment, and ensure equitable access to life-saving and life-changing therapies. Care coordination, medication assistance, and patient navigation are essential for helping patients navigate a complex healthcare system.  However, these services aren't reimbursed through traditional payment structures. 340B savings allow Ohio State to provide these services directly to patients, reducing patients' out-of-pocket costs and ensuring treatment is delivered as seamlessly as possible.

340B savings are reinvested in clinical operations that determine which services are available and at what capacity. At Ohio State, this translates into measurable impacts on access and care delivery across several dimensions.  340B savings support staffing levels and service capacity, enabling Ohio State to operate programs such as behavioral health, high-risk obstetrics, and trauma-level emergency care at volumes that Medicaid and Medicare reimbursement alone would not sustain. For patients who depend on these services, the practical outcome is access to care that would otherwise require traveling to another region or going without. 340B program savings help support many essential functions that are underfunded by Medicare, Medicaid, and other federal and state level funding programs for research and teaching.

answer_as_filed:
"Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B Drug Pricing Program to continue to provide the highest quality care for the communities we serve. By lowering the cost of eligible outpatient medications, 340B helps us redirect resources into patient care, pharmacy access and essential services for people who might otherwise have limited access to treatment. For Cleveland Clinic, 340B helps us stretch limited resources so we can continue serving as a safety net for highly specialized care, while also supporting patients experiencing unmet needs.
Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B benefit to help provide access to care, preserve access points and reinvest in broader community health efforts. In 2024 alone (the most recent year for which complete data are available), we provided $337.7 million in free or discounted care to more than 139,000 patients, contributed $1.49 billion in community benefit across Ohio, Florida and Nevada, and provided $28.7 million in subsidized health services that meet important community needs despite operating at a loss.
340B also helps Cleveland Clinic maintain pharmacy access and reduce barriers to medication adherence. Examples include operating 27 retail pharmacy locations across Northeast Ohio, opening a new community pharmacy at South Pointe Hospital in 2025, delivering, at no delivery cost, discharge prescriptions to patients and providing transition-of-care pharmacist support for patients after discharge.
For more information on how Cleveland Clinic uses 340B savings please visit our website at https://my.clevelandclinic.org/about/community/reports/340b-program
"

answer_as_filed:
The Bellevue Hospital does not place 340B financial benefits into a separately restricted account or directly assign those benefits to individual programs or expenses. Rather, the savings generated through the 340B Program are incorporated into the Hospital’s overall operating resources and support its ability to fulfill its charitable mission.

The 340B Program helps The Bellevue Hospital offset costs related to:

Charity care provided to uninsured and underinsured patients;
Unreimbursed and under-reimbursed services provided to Medicaid & Medicare beneficiaries; and
Essential hospital services that may not otherwise be financially sustainable


Because 340B financial benefits are integrated into the Hospital’s overall operations, they cannot be traced to specific expenditures on a dollar-for-dollar basis. However, these benefits strengthen the Hospital’s ability to manage uncompensated care costs, maintain essential services, and continue providing access to care for residents of Bellevue and the surrounding communities.

answer_as_filed: Kettering Health participates in the federal 340B Drug Pricing Program as part of its commitment to improving the health and well-being of the communities it serves. The program allows eligible Kettering Health entities to purchase outpatient medications at reduced prices, generating savings that are reinvested to expand access to care, improve affordability, and strengthen patient services.

Consistent with federal guidance, 340B savings are not maintained as a separate fund but are integrated into the overall financial framework of Kettering Health. These resources are strategically deployed to directly support patient care initiatives, particularly for underserved, uninsured, and underinsured populations.
Demonstrated Patient and Community Impact in 2025

In 2025, Kettering Health’s patient assistance program supported in part by 340B savings—generated over $91.8 million in total patient support, reflecting a substantial investment in medication access and affordability.
Complementing these efforts, Kettering Health also provided significant levels of uncompensated care across the system, underscoring its role as a safety net provider:
These figures highlight the magnitude of financial support provided to patients and communities and reinforce the critical role 340B savings play in sustaining these efforts.
Infusion Support: More than $29.3 million in assistance
Specialty Pharmacy Programs: Over $48.5 million in total support
Together, these investments demonstrate how 340B-enabled resources are directly translated into meaningful financial relief and improved access to care.

Kettering Health uses 340B program savings to broaden access to essential healthcare services. These resources help offset the significant financial burden reflected in the $376.5 million in uncompensated care provided in 2025, enabling:
Continued care regardless of a patient’s ability to pay
Expansion of services in rural and underserved communities
Sustainability of critical programs that operate at a financial loss
Medication affordability remains a central focus of Kettering Health’s 340B strategy. The 2025 data reflect a comprehensive approach that includes:
Direct financial assistance to reduce patient out-of-pocket costs
Free drug replacement programs ensuring continuity of therapy
Copay support for high-cost infusion and specialty medications
Innovative tools such as the 340B Care Card program
These efforts reduce financial barriers and complement the system’s broader charity care and uncompensated care commitments.
The breadth of assistance across infusion, specialty, and ambulatory care settings reflects Kettering Health’s investment in comprehensive clinical services. 340B savings help support:
Advanced therapies for complex and chronic conditions
Specialty pharmacy management of high-cost medications
These services are essential in managing the needs of patients who may otherwise contribute to uncompensated care if access were limited.

Kettering Health recognizes that financial hardship is a major barrier to care. The combination of $91.8 million in patient assistance and $376.5 million in uncompensated care demonstrates a system-wide commitment to reducing these barriers.
Additional support includes transportation, education, and care coordination services that ensure patients can access and adhere to treatment.
Delivering this level of patient and community support requires significant operational investment. 340B savings fund:
Clinical pharmacy teams and patient assistance coordinators
Infrastructure supporting specialty and infusion services
Technology systems for tracking and optimizing assistance
Offsetting Financial Pressures and Sustaining Services
The scale of charity care and bad debt in 2025 illustrates the financial realities faced by Kettering Health. 340B savings help offset:
$255.6 million in charity care provided to patients in need
$128.6 million in bad debt associated with unpaid care
These resources are essential to sustaining access to care and maintaining critical services across the system.
Through strategic reinvestment of 340B savings, Kettering Health continues to improve community health outcomes by:
Reducing delays in care due to financial barriers
Kettering Health is committed to responsible stewardship of the 340B program. Program savings support:
Policies and systems aligned with federal requirements

answer_as_filed:
Good Samaritan Hospital uses savings associated with participation in the 340B Drug Pricing Program to support patient care, community benefit activities, and services for vulnerable populations. These savings allow the hospital to stretch limited healthcare resources and reinvest in programs and services that improve access to care for uninsured, underinsured, low-income, and medically vulnerable patients.
Through this reinvestment, Good Samaritan Hospital is able to sustain charity care and uncompensated care provided throughout the hospital, while also supporting programs that address barriers to healthcare access and improve health outcomes. These resources help support Free Medical Clinic services, behavioral health services, maternal and perinatal care programs, OB/GYN and primary care services for at-risk populations, community outreach and screening programs, care management and patient navigation, medication assistance for financially vulnerable patients, transportation or social services support, and other community-focused initiatives that serve patients who may otherwise face significant financial, social, or clinical barriers to care.
The 340B program is vital to Good Samaritan Hospital’s ability to meet the needs of the community it serves. Savings generated through the program help preserve access to essential services that may be financially difficult to sustain but are necessary to support vulnerable patients and advance community health. These services include care provided to patients regardless of ability to pay, programs that improve access to preventive, primary, maternal, behavioral health, and specialty care, and support for patients with complex medical, financial, and social needs.
By reinvesting 340B savings into patient care and community health priorities, Good Samaritan Hospital is able to extend the impact of limited healthcare dollars, reduce barriers to care, and support services that improve access, continuity of care, and health outcomes for the community. The program remains an important tool that helps the hospital fulfill its mission and continue serving patients and populations with significant healthcare needs.

The Value of the 340B Program to Our Rural Hospital and Community 

 

Executive Summary 
The 340B Drug Pricing Program is a critical source of financial support that enables our hospital to continue fulfilling its mission of providing high-quality healthcare services to all patients regardless of their ability to pay. The savings generated through participation in the 340B program are not retained as profit; rather, they are reinvested directly into patient care, community health programs, capital improvements, and services that would otherwise be financially unsustainable in a rural healthcare environment. 

Supporting Oncology Services 

Cancer care requires significant investments in specialized staff, medications, equipment, and patient support services. 340B savings help offset the increasing costs associated with providing oncology services, allowing patients in our community to receive treatment closer to home rather than traveling to larger metropolitan areas. These savings support access to life-saving therapies, patient navigation, and comprehensive care for vulnerable populations. 

Funding Withdrawal Management Services 

Our Withdrawal Management program serves a disproportionately high Medicaid population and operates at a financial loss. Despite the negative margin, the service was identified as a critical need through our Community Health Needs Assessment. 340B savings help support the continuation of this essential program, ensuring individuals struggling with substance use disorders have access to treatment, recovery support, and care coordination within our community. 

Supporting Charity Care and Uncompensated Care 

Many patients do not qualify for Medicaid or formal charity care programs yet still lack the financial resources to pay for needed medical services. 340B savings help offset uncompensated and undercompensated care, allowing our hospital to continue serving patients regardless of financial circumstance while reducing barriers to care. 

Offsetting Declining Reimbursement 

Hospitals continue to face increasing financial pressure from reductions and inadequacies in reimbursement from Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial managed care organizations. Reimbursement rates often fail to cover the actual cost of delivering care, particularly for rural providers. The 340B program helps bridge a portion of this gap, supporting the financial stability necessary to maintain access to essential services. 

Reinvestment in Hospital Infrastructure and Technology 

340B savings allow the hospital to reinvest in critical infrastructure and patient care improvements. These investments include new medical equipment, modernization projects, facility repairs, technology upgrades, cybersecurity initiatives, and other improvements that enhance quality, safety, and patient experience. Without these savings, many capital projects would be delayed or eliminated. 

Protecting Access to Care in a Rural Community 

As a rural healthcare provider, we operate in an environment with unique challenges, including lower patient volumes, workforce shortages, transportation barriers, and limited access to specialty care. Compared with the neighboring Columbus metropolitan area, our community has fewer healthcare resources readily available. The 340B program helps ensure local residents maintain access to services close to home and supports the development of future programs identified as community needs. 

Conclusion 

The 340B Program is an essential tool that enables our hospital to fulfill its obligation to serve the healthcare needs of our community. Program savings strengthen access to oncology care, sustain withdrawal management services, support charity and uncompensated care, mitigate reimbursement challenges, fund necessary capital investments, and preserve access to healthcare in our rural region. Continued participation in the 340B program directly benefits patients and helps ensure the long-term viability of services that our community depends upon every day.

answer_as_filed: Trinity Hospital Holding Company is Disproportionate Share Hospital, part of the Trinity Health System located in Steubenville, Ohio. We are located in a federally designated Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA). Trinity Hospital provides care to a service area of just over 200,000 individuals. Despite operating at a significant loss, Trinity provides over $17 million in net community benefits including health improvement services, professional education, as well as financial assistance to uninsured or under insured patients. The 340B program helps offset these costs. The program supports our Outpatient Infusion Center, which provides comprehensive cancer care, chemotherapy and non-oncology infusion services in the patient’s home community. It also helps fund a clinical pharmacist that works in patient care areas to improve medication outcomes.

Our 340B Story

About Avita Health System

Avita Health System is a nonprofit, patient-centered health care system in North Central Ohio. It was established in 2011 as the parent company of Bucyrus and Galion Hospitals. In 2017, Avita opened its third hospital, located in Ontario, and now has over 40 clinics and service locations in Crawford and Richland counties with more than 150 employed medical providers, 1,000 affiliated medical providers, and 2,400 employees. Avita services 9 counties with populations totaling over 500,000 Ohioans. Avita’s mission is to improve the health and well-being of those we serve by providing exceptional patient experiences across the continuum of care and consistently exceeding national benchmarks for quality, care, and service.  Unique to the area, Avita is an independent, locally governed health care system with a board of directors that live in the communities where health services are provided.  As a nonprofit health system, Avita values charitable giving and provided over $48 million in uncompensated, unreimbursed, and charity care in FY2025. 

Benefits of the 340B Program

Avita Health System relies on the 340B Drug Pricing Program in order to “stretch scarce Federal resources as far as possible, reaching more eligible patients and providing more comprehensive care”, as Congress had originally intended.  The 340B program is funded entirely through drug manufacturer discounts and there is no cost to the taxpayer or community.  The 340B program is critical to ensuring Avita’s role as a safety-net community hospital, thereby providing vital access to comprehensive and life-saving health services, programs, and prescription drugs.  Savings realized through participation in the 340B program are reinvested into Avita Health System’s internal programs and services, or the expansion of external community assistance programs.  These programs and services include, but are not limited to:

The 340B program enables Avita Health System to expand access to medications across the continuum of care. 
•	Maintaining formulary access to critical medications that, without 340B discounts, could not be sustainably offered due to reimbursement rates below acquisition costs
•	Patient access to ultra high cost specialty pharmaceuticals and infusions, including immunotherapy, bispecifics, and radioligand therapy at our infusion centers and comprehensive cancer center
•	Subsidizing chemotherapy and immunotherapy for uninsured and underinsured patients
•	Providing pediatric vaccines at all pediatrician and family medicine physician practices system-wide, including continuing a neonatal Hepatitis B vaccination program that provides the birth dose at no charge to patients 
•	Expanding access to outpatient pharmacy services through a second entity-owned retail pharmacy in Crestline, Ohio, restoring essential pharmaceutical care to a community that had become a pharmacy desert. 

The 340B Program enables Avita Health System to stretch scarce federal resources as far as possible, reaching more eligible patients and providing more comprehensive services.

•	Maintaining community access to 24/7 critical services including emergency medicine (ER), inpatient care, surgery, advanced imaging, and intensive care at all three Avita Health System hospitals
•	Continuing our commitment to women’s health and perinatal care by continuing to provide Maternity & Obstetric services in Crawford County, while expanding services in Richland County 
•	Expanding access to specialized services and medical expertise, such as cardiac catheterization, inpatient hemodialysis/CRRT, and telestroke medicine 
•	Providing critical support for ICU and Med/Surg patients with pulmonologists, intensivists, nephrologists, neurologists, cardiologists, and other specialists that enable patients to receive care close to home, without transferring out of the system. 
•	Expanding outpatient access to specialty medical and surgical services in our rural, Critical Access Hospitals, including rheumatology, urology, orthopedics, spinal surgery, gastroenterology, pain management, ENT, and wound care (including hyperbaric oxygen treatment) allowing patients to receive expert care close to home
•	Access to adult and pediatric occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech therapy and audiology services
•	Expanding access to state-of-the-art technology, including robotic surgery, 3D mammography, 3T MRI, and LINAC with RapidArc® Dynamic planning.
•	Expanding cancer care for our communities through medical oncology and infusion services at all three Avita Heath System hospitals and a new, state-of-the-art comprehensive Cancer Center in Richland County offering radiation oncology services in addition to medical oncology and infusion. 
•	Nurse navigation services for oncology patients to guide them through their cancer care journey
•	Access to charity and indigent care programs, as well as financial assistance for basic medical services, oncology and other specialty medications
•	Access to patient billing advocates and financial counselors to assist with needs beyond direct medical care, such as gas, electricity, transportation, etc.
•	Absorbing waived self-administered drug charges for Medicare observation patients
•	Outpatient social work services to support patients with psychosocial needs and care coordination
•	Access to psychiatric and addiction medicine services for patients with mental health and substance use disorders.
•	Crisis intervention services for patients experiencing mental health or behavioral health emergencies
•	Access to full service Home Health and Hospice care across an 8 county region, including inpatient hospice and respite care. 
•	Providing ambulatory clinical pharmacy services (Medication Therapy Management clinics) to at-risk patients to improve medication adherence and outcomes through disease state management
•	Expanding access to patient assistance programs through pharmacist coordinated Medication Access Programs and Drug Repository Services 
•	Partnerships with local communities to provide community health improvement services, such as diabetes prevention, prenatal support, and tobacco cessation
•	Offer free sports physicals for the community and access to athletic training services to school districts in local and surrounding counties
•	Sensory kits for neurodivergent pediatric patients in the Emergency Department to support their comfort and care experience
•	24/7 access to forensic services, including free medical screenings and exams for victims of sexual assault and abuse, child abuse, domestic violence, human trafficking, and other criminal offenses for victims in Crawford, Richland, and surrounding counties. 
•	Access to 365 day Walk In Clinic services at 3 separate locations across Richland county.
•	Access to pre-employment evaluations, post-accident services, and training programs for local employers through our WorkWell Occupational Health services.
•	Staff tuition assistance and subsidy programs to support continuing education and professional development
•	Nurse education partnerships with local nursing schools, enabling staff to complete nursing school at no cost to them, strengthening our workforce and community

Impact of Scaling back the 340B Program

Avita Health System is committed to our mission of improving the health and wellbeing of those we serve. We fulfill our mission primarily through the services and programs that we offer our patients, as well as through the support that we give to our communities. Scaling back the 340B Program would threaten our capacity to maintain access to the full scope of medications and services described above, jeopardizing essential care in our rural communities where healthcare options are already limited.

answer_as_filed:
340B savings help support University Hospitals’ overall capacity to provide community benefit, which totaled $511 million in 2024. These resources play an important role in sustaining a wide range of programs and services that benefit our patients and community. These supports include:

Financial assistance for patients who are unable to afford hospital care, physician care and/or medications
Medication access services to help patients navigate insurance requirements and reduce financial barriers
Patient engagement programs focused on refill management and improving adherence to therapy
Clinical services, including pharmacists embedded in provider offices and ongoing care management
Education and training by preparing future generations of caregivers
Transportation assistance
Home health services
Community outreach initiatives
Medicaid shortfall and other uncompensated care
Support for medical research
In-kind contributions to community organizations

answer_as_filed: The Stark County Health Department received federal Title X funding through the Ohio Department of Health Family Planning Program to support essential reproductive health services. As part of this program, the department operated as a 340B covered entity, allowing it to access medications at significantly reduced costs. This designation enabled the clinic to stretch limited resources and expand access to care for vulnerable populations. Utilizing 340B pricing, the Title X clinic was able to purchase contraceptives and related medications at a discounted rate. These medications were then provided free of charge to uninsured and underinsured clients in accordance with Title X program guidelines.

(Narrative) Provide additional detail/context as necessary:
answer_as_filed: LCHD only purchases 340B drugs to the extent necessary for its federally funded Reproductive Health and Wellness Grant. If the grant were to have a profit, it is likely that the funding would have to be returned to the Ohio Department of Health, who would then return the funds to the Department of Health and Human Services. For the efficient use of funds, and to provide maximum value to patients, LCHD operates the program in a manner that breaks even with its costs. Since there are no 340b profits to report, there is no detailed accounting record of expenditures from 340B profits. To the extent that LCHD earns revenue from providing 340B services, the revenues are credited to fund E02 Family Planning Fund (i.e. Reproductive Health and Wellness Grant). Program income is reported on a monthly basis to the Ohio Department of Health. Detailed records of the revenues and expenditures of the Reproductive Health Grant are available upon request. 340B funds are not separately tracked in the County's accounting records.

answer_as_filed: As a 340B Covered Entity, Shawnee uses savings generated through participation in the 340B Drug Pricing Program to support and strengthen our mission of providing comprehensive healthcare and supportive services to underserved and vulnerable populations.  The program enable us to stretch scarce federal resources, allowing us to expand access to care, improve patient outcomes, and maintain critical services that would otherwise be financially challenging to sustain.  Our 340B savings are reinvested directly into the operations and infrastructure necessary to serve our patient population.  These expenditures support both healthcare delivery and the social determinants of health that significantly inpact patient well-being.  A portion of our 340B funds is used to support essential operational expenses and facility improvements that ensure a safe, reliable, and efficient environment for patient care.  These investments include major capital projects such as the replacement and maintenance of HVAC systems, which help maintain proper environmental conditions for patient services, staff operations, and medication storage and the staff that support these functions.  This fiscal year alone, we have had to repair a large parking lot, install three HVAC systems, and fix a roof on our largest clinic.  We also utilize 340B funds for vehicle purchases and maintenance necessary to support transportation services, home visits, medication delivery, and other community-based programs.                                                                    Pharmacy Operations:  340B program savings help offset pharmacy expenses that are not fully covered by Medicaid or other reimbursement sources.  This includes pharmacy staff salaries and fringe benefits for pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, and support personnel who are essential to medication management, patient counseling, prescription processing, and compliance activities.  Byu funding these positions, we are able to maintain pharmacy services that improve medication access, adherence, and overall patient outcomes.  Additionally, 340B funds support pharmacy courier services that facilitate medication delivery to patients who may face transportation barriers, mobility limitations, or geographic challenges.  These services help ensure timely access to medications and reduce interruptions in treatment.  Transportation Services:  Transportation is a significant barrier to healthcare access for many of our patients.  To address this need, we use 340B savings to support transportation drivers and transportation-related services that enable patgients to attend medical appointments, obtain medications, and access other necessary healthcare and community services.  These programs help reduce missed appointments, improve continuity of care, and support better health outcomes.  We have purchased four vehicles that are used to enhance access.  Recognizing that stable housing is a critical component of health, we invest 340B resources in housing support services.  Housing aides assist patients with housing-related needs, helping them maintain stable living environments and access supportive resources.  These services are particularly important for individuals facing economic hardship, chronic illness, behavioral health challenges, or other complex needs that can affect their ability to achieve and maintain optimal health outcomes.

Other internal costs: Transporter Wages and fuel/maintenance for drug delivery and paitent transportation, license renewal, insurance and maint & repair

answer_as_filed:
How 340B Savings Support MetroHealth Patients:
 
The MetroHealth System is Cuyahoga County's public safety-net health system, caring for more than 300,000 patients regardless of their ability to pay. MetroHealth participates in the 340B Program with services provided through two types of covered entities: MetroHealth Medical Center, a disproportionate share hospital (DSH), and MetroHealth Community Health Centers, a federally qualified health center (FQHC). The benefits described below reflect the coordinated work of both covered entities to provide comprehensive patient care services to the region. Public hospitals and Community Health Centers like ours care for the community's most medically and socially vulnerable, low-income residents. They are exactly the providers Congress intended to benefit when it created the 340B Program. MetroHealth Medical Center was the second hospital in Ohio to join the program, in early 1994.
 
Our patients face barriers to health that extend well beyond the exam room: 22% experience housing instability, 22% face food insecurity, 13% deal with transportation insecurity, and 17.5% live below the federal poverty level. More than two-thirds rely on government insurance programs like Medicaid or Medicare, or are uninsured.
 
340B savings allow MetroHealth to stretch limited resources further and reinvest them in care and services that would otherwise be reduced or unavailable. Most importantly, the program lets us bring life-saving medications and outpatient care to the neighborhoods where our patients live. That keeps people out of the emergency department and lowers the risk that their conditions become life-threatening. Because of 340B, MetroHealth is:
 
• Making medications affordable: MetroHealth offers four levels of financial assistance for Cuyahoga County residents with incomes up to 400% of the federal poverty level. These plans provide comprehensive care, including prescription drugs, at no cost or at a steeply discounted cost. Patients who don't qualify can receive vouchers and copay assistance to lower what they pay at the pharmacy. Our financial assistance coordinators also help any patient find lower-cost medications, manufacturer assistance and other programs. They also help patients get specialty drugs for cancer, HIV, hepatitis C, rheumatologic and cardiovascular conditions at affordable prices. Last year, that work saved patients more than $52 million. And because our pharmacy prices average 25–30% below other retail pharmacies, we lower costs for payers as well.
 
• Getting patients on treatment faster: For specialty and high-cost medications, insurance approvals are often what delays care. MetroHealth's Specialty Pharmacy and centralized prior authorization call center take that work on. They handle insurer requirements, secure approvals and find financial assistance. In 2025, the team completed 54,250 prior authorizations with an average turnaround of about 18 hours. Patients start therapy sooner and stay on it, and our providers can spend their time treating patients instead of doing paperwork.
 
• Bringing care into the neighborhoods: Our more than 20 outpatient locations across Cleveland and Cuyahoga County offer primary and specialty care, dental, vision and behavioral health services for all ages. Patients who qualify receive this care free or at significantly reduced cost. These sites keep people healthy and out of the hospital, but the network runs at a significant financial loss, which 340B savings help offset.
 
• Expanding pharmacy access: MetroHealth operates twelve community retail pharmacies in neighborhoods where our patients live, including areas that became pharmacy deserts when chain pharmacies closed. These locations offer free vaccinations and no-cost home delivery. At our main campus, a 24/7 pharmacy with drive-through service is open to anyone in the community who needs medication after an Emergency Department visit, after hours, or when other pharmacies are closed.
 
• Putting pharmacists on the care team: MetroHealth embeds pharmacists in clinical areas as part of our inpatient and ambulatory care teams. There they work directly with patients and adjust treatment as needs change, improving health outcomes.
 
• Sending patients home with their medications: Our bedside delivery program brings prescriptions to patients before discharge, so they don't need an extra trip to the pharmacy. No-cost home delivery continues after they get home. For patients with transportation, mobility or other barriers, this makes it far more likely they start and stay on their medications. That helps prevent complications and avoidable return visits to the hospital. Delivery also supports our antimicrobial stewardship efforts. When culture results or clinical review show that a patient needs a different antibiotic after discharge, our pharmacy team coordinates the change and delivers the new antibiotic to the patient's home the same day.
 
• Supporting mothers, babies and families: MetroHealth partners with the community to improve maternal and infant health and reduce infant mortality. 340B savings have helped expand access to midwives and doulas, home visits through our Nurse-Family Partnership team, and CenteringPregnancy programs that support pregnant women early and often throughout pregnancy.
 
• Keeping care going through crises: 340B resources helped MetroHealth maintain access to medications and uninterrupted care through major disruptions. These included the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2024 Change Healthcare cyberattack, which disrupted pharmacy services nationwide.
 
• Caring for patients who have nowhere else to turn: In 2025, MetroHealth provided $358 million in charity care, nearly $1 million every day. 340B savings give a public safety-net system the financial flexibility to keep offering Level I trauma care, adult and pediatric burn care, primary and specialty care, and other essential services to everyone, regardless of ability to pay.
 
Without 340B savings, MetroHealth would have far fewer resources to sustain these services, and the impact would reach well beyond the pharmacy counter. Financial assistance, neighborhood clinics, pharmacy access and the programs that help patients overcome barriers to care would all come under pressure. For many of our patients, 340B is the difference between getting care close to home and getting care only in an emergency room.

answer_as_filed: Alliance Family Health Center is a Federally Qualified Health Center Look-Alike, serving a medically underserved community without the benefit of annual Section 330 Health Center Program (New Access Point) grant funding. Unlike many federally funded health centers, AFHC must sustain its mission primarily through patient service revenue, strategic partnerships, grants, and responsible stewardship of programs such as 340B.  The 340B Program is not simply a pharmacy program, it is an essential component of our ability to fulfill our mission. Savings generated through the program are reinvested directly into the operation of the health center, allowing AFHC to expand access to comprehensive primary care, women's health, behavioral health, pharmacy services, care coordination, and other enabling services for patients regardless of their ability to pay. Since becoming a Look-Alike, AFHC has navigated extraordinary challenges, including the COVID-19 pandemic, while continuing to grow access to care, expand services, and strengthen the healthcare safety net within our community. Despite not receiving an opportunity to apply for a New Access Point award since 2019, the organization has remained financially responsible, expanded patient access, and continued investing in quality improvement, workforce development, compliance, and innovative programs designed to meet community needs. Every dollar generated through the 340B Program is reinvested into our mission. These resources help offset the cost of caring for uninsured and underinsured patients, support the infrastructure required to operate a comprehensive community health center, and enable AFHC to continue delivering high-quality, accessible healthcare to the patients and families who rely on us every day.

answer_as_filed: Alliance Family Health Center does not segregate 340B savings into a separate fund. Consistent with HRSA guidance, 340B program savings are incorporated into the organization's operating revenue and are used to support the health center's mission of providing comprehensive healthcare services to medically underserved populations. Savings help offset the costs of uncompensated care, expanded access to services, workforce, quality improvement activities, and other operating expenses necessary to maintain and enhance patient care.

- Pediatric HTC to Adult HTC Transition Services.

Introduction:
The 340B Drug Pricing Program intends to enable covered entities to stretch scarce federal resources as far as possible, reaching more eligible patients and providing more comprehensive services. For Nationwide Children's, this program is critical to supporting our mission of providing the highest quality of care to all children and their families, regardless of their ability to pay. The 340B savings achieved through our Hemostasis and Thrombosis Center are reinvested directly into care and advocacy for our patient population. 
Comprehensive Care Model:
Through 340B savings, the Hemostasis and Thrombosis Center at Nationwide Children’s Hospital is able to offer a comprehensive care model that serves as a one-stop-shop for patients and families with bleeding and clotting disorders.  This model includes a multidisciplinary team of physicians, nurse practitioners, nurse clinicians, nurses, genetic counselors, psychologists, pharmacists, dental hygienists, psychologists, among others.  These disciplines work collaboratively to ensure the best possible outcomes and experience for patients and their families.
Additionally, Nationwide Children’s is home to one of the oldest Young Women’s Hematology clinics in the country, combining expertise in hemostasis-thrombosis and adolescent medicine.  This specialized clinic provides a compassionate, patient-centered approach for adolescent girls with suspected bleeding and clotting disorders and offers advanced diagnostic and treatment options for those experiencing heavy menstrual bleeding.
Professional Education and Training:
The education and development of hemostasis and thrombosis experts is also a top priority.  Nationwide Children’s Hospital offers a fourth-year fellowship for physicians seeking to expand their expertise in hemostasis and thrombosis, helping to address a growing workforce shortage of adequately trained physicians in this field.  Fellows complete a comprehensive curriculum including, outpatient clinical care, inpatient service, research, quality improvement, teaching opportunities, and select elective rotations.
Research:
Research is a central focus of the Hemostasis and Thrombosis Center at Nationwide Children’s.  HTC funds are currently being reserved for a research study evaluating a new treatment for rare congenital bleeding disorders.  The study aims to assess the effectiveness of a drug in mice that blocks a protein responsible for slowing down blood clotting.  By blocking this protein, the body can produce more thrombin, a key enzyme that helps blood clot.  If successful in mice, this research could lead to a new treatment option for individuals with rare congenital bleeding disorders, potentially reducing the need for therapies that require blood transfusions.  This project is currently under review by HRSA. 
Laboratory Medicine:
The Hemostasis and Thrombosis Center at Nationwide Children’s Hospital has invested in a Director of Hemostasis and Thrombosis Testing within the Division of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine.  This position is responsible for reviewing and interpreting lab tests related to bleeding and clotting conditions, diagnosing new cases of hemophilia, identifying other congenital or acquired coagulopathies, detecting and quantifying acquired inhibitors, and advising on approaches to multiple factor concentrate monitoring. The role also includes interpretation of platelet function testing and the detection and diagnosis of both acquired and congenital thrombophilia.  Additionally, the Director collaborates closely with hematology physician partners to assess the feasibility of introducing new laboratory tests. 
This role also has an important teaching component, providing education to residents and fellows on laboratory administration, how lab tests for bleeding and clotting work, how medications that affect clotting are monitored, and how lab results guide decisions about blood transfusions and patient treatment.
Community Outreach and Education:
The Hemostasis and Thrombosis Center at Nationwide Children’s is a recipient of a grant from the CASCADE Hemophilia Consortium, enabling the Center to provide additional support to patients and families in need.  This includes assistance with medical expenses, transportation, among other items.  
Nationwide Children’s also hosts a Family Education Day at the Columbus Zoo for patients with bleeding disorders and their families.  This event covers a wide range of topics, including infusion education, mental health, genetics, and transitioning from pediatric to adult healthcare providers.  Additional sessions address school-related concerns, finding additional community resources, available hemophilia camps for children and young adults, and navigating health insurance.  
School outreach is another key priority.  The Hemophilia and Thrombosis Center team provides education to daycare, preschool, and school staff on hemophilia and strategies to support students with bleeding disorders in educational settings.
Our staff also partner with the Greater Ohio Bleeding Disorders Foundation, providing community education at local events.  
Finally, Nationwide Children’s supports FAMOHIO, an organization that hosts an Education Weekend for individuals and families affected by bleeding disorders.

answer_as_filed:
The Comprehensive Hemophilia Treatment Center (HTC) at University Hospitals is a 340B Covered Entity that utilizes funds generated through its 340B program to offer programs and services that benefit our patients and other members of the bleeding disorder community. These programs and services include:
•	Medication access and care coordination services to help patients navigate insurance requirements, reduce financial barriers, and coordinate specialty care
•	Patient engagement programs focused on refill management and improving adherence to treatment plans
•	Education & Training for multi-disciplinary HTC staff members to ensure best possible care for patients
•	Transportation and Access to Care assistance
•	Home Health Services
•	Community Outreach & Education Initiatives
•	In-kind contributions to community organizations
Through these efforts, our Hemophilia Treatment Center enhances access to comprehensive care, improves health outcomes, reduces barriers to treatment, and provides meaningful community benefit for individuals and families affected by bleeding disorders. Participation in the 340B Program enables our organization to strengthen services that support the long-term health and well-being of patients across Northeast Ohio.

answer_as_filed: The Ryan White Part C grant provides services to all Ryan White eligible patients. Patients currently enrolled in the Ryan White program are eligible for medication and copay support, transportation vouchers, as well as medical, lab, dental,  and psychosocial services provided by staff supported by program income from 340B revenue. Part C funds also support the Men's support group,  Patient Advisory Board and Annual Patient Picnic  as well as community outreach at public events like PRIDE and World AIDS Day. We also host regularly scheduled events at local libraries and community centers  that provide free HIV testing  and  link patients to care and resources. Ryan White grant programs are audited annually for program integrity both internally and by the funding source.

answer_as_filed:
Cincinnati Children’s relies on the 340B program to extend limited resources, preserve access to essential pediatric services, and support children and families who face financial, medical, and geographic barriers to care.
Cincinnati Children’s Hospital is a nonprofit, comprehensive pediatric health system.  It is one of the 5 largest U.S. Children’s hospital.  The hospital plays a critical role in serving the broader Cincinnati region, which includes communities in Kentucky and Indiana.  Our hospital uses the savings generated from 340B medications to support a broad range of community benefit activities that are otherwise financially difficult to sustain. The program allows our hospital to stretch limited resources and reinvest those savings into services that address unmet health needs, particularly for low-income, uninsured, underinsured, and medically vulnerable populations.
Cincinnati Children’s is committed to providing care to everyone in need, regardless of ability to pay. That commitment is especially important in Cincinnati, where median household income is 35% lower than the national average and 20% of children live in households below the poverty line. Nearly half of the care Cincinnati Children’s provides is for Medicaid enrollees, and Medicaid reimbursement falls more than 35% below the hospital’s cost of care. These factors make 340B savings essential to sustaining access for children and families who rely on Cincinnati Children’s.
340B savings help Cincinnati Children’s expand access to care by supporting free and reduced-cost services, charity care programs, medication assistance, and care coordination for patients with complex medical and mental health needs. These resources also help maintain clinics in underserved areas and provide over-the-counter medications at no charge, which can prevent avoidable emergency room visits. Cincinnati Children’s further advances access by partnering with local school districts to develop school-based health centers in communities where socioeconomic barriers make regular well-care and treatment for acute illnesses more difficult to obtain. The discounts received through the 340B program help deliver care at a lower cost to patients and families.
Cincinnati Children’s hospital-based specialty pharmacy provides medications and support for patients with complex, chronic, or rare conditions. Specialty medications are typically high-cost and often require specialized handling, administration, and ongoing coordination. Because 70% of Cincinnati Children’s specialty pharmacy patients are Medicaid enrollees, the hospital provides additional support, including home nursing services that are often not reimbursed. Discounts provided through the 340B program are vital to maintaining the full spectrum of specialty pharmacy services for patients, regardless of ability to pay.
Cincinnati Children’s provides cell and gene therapies to patients.  Providing cell and gene therapies to pediatric patients creates significant clinical responsibilities and time-consuming administrative processes. When these therapies are covered by Medicaid or commercial insurance, reimbursement often does not reflect the full cost of providing them. These therapies can cost several million dollars, and the hospital may need to pay those costs months before reimbursement is received. Without the savings provided by the 340B program, CCHMC’s ability to purchase and administer these therapies would be limited.

answer_as_filed:
340B savings help support University Hospitals’ overall capacity to provide community benefit, which totaled $511 million in 2024. These resources play an important role in sustaining a wide range of programs and services that benefit our patients and community. These supports include:

Financial assistance for patients who are unable to afford hospital care, physician care and/or medications
Medication access services to help patients navigate insurance requirements and reduce financial barriers
Patient engagement programs focused on refill management and improving adherence to therapy
Clinical services, including pharmacists embedded in provider offices and ongoing care management
Education and training by preparing future generations of caregivers
Transportation assistance
Home health services
Community outreach initiatives
Medicaid shortfall and other uncompensated care
Support for medical research
In-kind contributions to community organizations

answer_as_filed:
"Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B Drug Pricing Program to continue to provide the highest quality care for the communities we serve. By lowering the cost of eligible outpatient medications, 340B helps us redirect resources into patient care, pharmacy access and essential services for people who might otherwise have limited access to treatment. For Cleveland Clinic, 340B helps us stretch limited resources so we can continue serving as a safety net for highly specialized care, while also supporting patients experiencing unmet needs.
Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B benefit to help provide access to care, preserve access points and reinvest in broader community health efforts. In 2024 alone (the most recent year for which complete data are available), we provided $337.7 million in free or discounted care to more than 139,000 patients, contributed $1.49 billion in community benefit across Ohio, Florida and Nevada, and provided $28.7 million in subsidized health services that meet important community needs despite operating at a loss.
340B also helps Cleveland Clinic maintain pharmacy access and reduce barriers to medication adherence. Examples include operating 27 retail pharmacy locations across Northeast Ohio, opening a new community pharmacy at South Pointe Hospital in 2025, delivering, at no delivery cost, discharge prescriptions to patients and providing transition-of-care pharmacist support for patients after discharge.
For more information on how Cleveland Clinic uses 340B savings please visit our website at https://my.clevelandclinic.org/about/community/reports/340b-program
"

answer_as_filed:
Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B Drug Pricing Program to continue to provide the highest quality care for the communities we serve. By lowering the cost of eligible outpatient medications, 340B helps us redirect resources into patient care, pharmacy access and essential services for people who might otherwise have limited access to treatment. For Cleveland Clinic, 340B helps us stretch limited resources so we can continue serving as a safety net for highly specialized care, while also supporting patients experiencing unmet needs.
Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B benefit to help provide access to care, preserve access points and reinvest in broader community health efforts. In 2024 alone (the most recent year for which complete data are available), we provided $337.7 million in free or discounted care to more than 139,000 patients, contributed $1.49 billion in community benefit across Ohio, Florida and Nevada, and provided $28.7 million in subsidized health services that meet important community needs despite operating at a loss.
340B also helps Cleveland Clinic maintain pharmacy access and reduce barriers to medication adherence. Examples include operating 27 retail pharmacy locations across Northeast Ohio, opening a new community pharmacy at South Pointe Hospital in 2025, delivering, at no delivery cost, discharge prescriptions to patients and providing transition-of-care pharmacist support for patients after discharge.
For more information on how Cleveland Clinic uses 340B savings please visit our website at https://my.clevelandclinic.org/about/community/reports/340b-program

answer_as_filed: Miami Valley Hospital and Atrium Medical Center qualify for the 340B program and collectively saved $69.9 million and $54.0 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively. 340B savings assist health systems in partially subsidizing services to patients that operate at a loss. Consistent with Premier Health’s mission, care is provided to patients regardless of the patient’s ability to pay. For patients who qualify as charity care based on their inability to pay, the estimated cost incurred by Premier Health to provide these services, less recognized charity care subsidies, was $31.4 million and $22.7 million for 2025 and 2024 respectively. Also consistent with Premier Health’s mission, services are provided to Medicare and Medicaid covered patients where payment is not sufficient to cover the cost of providing the service. The shortfall of payment to cost in unreimbursed Medicaid, Medicare and other means-tested government programs totaled $395.0 million and $449.8 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively. Premier Health also provided other community health improvement, community benefit and subsidized health services totaling $45.3 million and $86.1 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively. The savings from the 340B program play a critical role in ensuring access to many health services to patients regardless of their ability to pay, and the savings only cover a small portion of the overall unfunded and underfunded care provided across all patients.

answer_as_filed: Kettering Health participates in the federal 340B Drug Pricing Program as part of its commitment to improving the health and well-being of the communities it serves. The program allows eligible Kettering Health entities to purchase outpatient medications at reduced prices, generating savings that are reinvested to expand access to care, improve affordability, and strengthen patient services.

Consistent with federal guidance, 340B savings are not maintained as a separate fund but are integrated into the overall financial framework of Kettering Health. These resources are strategically deployed to directly support patient care initiatives, particularly for underserved, uninsured, and underinsured populations.
Demonstrated Patient and Community Impact in 2025

In 2025, Kettering Health’s patient assistance program supported in part by 340B savings—generated over $91.8 million in total patient support, reflecting a substantial investment in medication access and affordability.
Complementing these efforts, Kettering Health also provided significant levels of uncompensated care across the system, underscoring its role as a safety net provider:
These figures highlight the magnitude of financial support provided to patients and communities and reinforce the critical role 340B savings play in sustaining these efforts.
Infusion Support: More than $29.3 million in assistance
Specialty Pharmacy Programs: Over $48.5 million in total support
Together, these investments demonstrate how 340B-enabled resources are directly translated into meaningful financial relief and improved access to care.

Kettering Health uses 340B program savings to broaden access to essential healthcare services. These resources help offset the significant financial burden reflected in the $376.5 million in uncompensated care provided in 2025, enabling:
Continued care regardless of a patient’s ability to pay
Expansion of services in rural and underserved communities
Sustainability of critical programs that operate at a financial loss
Medication affordability remains a central focus of Kettering Health’s 340B strategy. The 2025 data reflect a comprehensive approach that includes:
Direct financial assistance to reduce patient out-of-pocket costs
Free drug replacement programs ensuring continuity of therapy
Copay support for high-cost infusion and specialty medications
Innovative tools such as the 340B Care Card program
These efforts reduce financial barriers and complement the system’s broader charity care and uncompensated care commitments.
The breadth of assistance across infusion, specialty, and ambulatory care settings reflects Kettering Health’s investment in comprehensive clinical services. 340B savings help support:
Advanced therapies for complex and chronic conditions
Specialty pharmacy management of high-cost medications
These services are essential in managing the needs of patients who may otherwise contribute to uncompensated care if access were limited.

Kettering Health recognizes that financial hardship is a major barrier to care. The combination of $91.8 million in patient assistance and $376.5 million in uncompensated care demonstrates a system-wide commitment to reducing these barriers.
Additional support includes transportation, education, and care coordination services that ensure patients can access and adhere to treatment.
Delivering this level of patient and community support requires significant operational investment. 340B savings fund:
Clinical pharmacy teams and patient assistance coordinators
Infrastructure supporting specialty and infusion services
Technology systems for tracking and optimizing assistance
Offsetting Financial Pressures and Sustaining Services
The scale of charity care and bad debt in 2025 illustrates the financial realities faced by Kettering Health. 340B savings help offset:
$255.6 million in charity care provided to patients in need
$128.6 million in bad debt associated with unpaid care
These resources are essential to sustaining access to care and maintaining critical services across the system.

Reducing delays in care due to financial barriers

answer_as_filed:
"Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B Drug Pricing Program to continue to provide the highest quality care for the communities we serve. By lowering the cost of eligible outpatient medications, 340B helps us redirect resources into patient care, pharmacy access and essential services for people who might otherwise have limited access to treatment. For Cleveland Clinic, 340B helps us stretch limited resources so we can continue serving as a safety net for highly specialized care, while also supporting patients experiencing unmet needs.
Cleveland Clinic uses the 340B benefit to help provide access to care, preserve access points and reinvest in broader community health efforts. In 2024 alone (the most recent year for which complete data are available), we provided $337.7 million in free or discounted care to more than 139,000 patients, contributed $1.49 billion in community benefit across Ohio, Florida and Nevada, and provided $28.7 million in subsidized health services that meet important community needs despite operating at a loss.
340B also helps Cleveland Clinic maintain pharmacy access and reduce barriers to medication adherence. Examples include operating 27 retail pharmacy locations across Northeast Ohio, opening a new community pharmacy at South Pointe Hospital in 2025, delivering, at no delivery cost, discharge prescriptions to patients and providing transition-of-care pharmacist support for patients after discharge.
For more information on how Cleveland Clinic uses 340B savings please visit our website at https://my.clevelandclinic.org/about/community/reports/340b-program
"
