answer_as_filed: Kettering Health participates in the federal 340B Drug Pricing Program as part of its commitment to improving the health and well-being of the communities it serves. The program allows eligible Kettering Health entities to purchase outpatient medications at reduced prices, generating savings that are reinvested to expand access to care, improve affordability, and strengthen patient services.

Consistent with federal guidance, 340B savings are not maintained as a separate fund but are integrated into the overall financial framework of Kettering Health. These resources are strategically deployed to directly support patient care initiatives, particularly for underserved, uninsured, and underinsured populations.
Demonstrated Patient and Community Impact in 2025

In 2025, Kettering Health’s patient assistance program supported in part by 340B savings—generated over $91.8 million in total patient support, reflecting a substantial investment in medication access and affordability.

answer_as_filed: The Ryan White Part D grant provides services to women and youth under 25. Patients currently enrolled in the Ryan White program are eligible for medication and copay support, transportation vouchers, as well as medical, lab, dental,  and psychosocial services provided by staff supported by program income from 340B revenue. Part D funds also support the Women's support group,  Youth support group and Yoga classes provided in our clinic space as well as community outreach at public events like PRIDE and World AIDS Day. We also host regularly scheduled events at local libraries and community centers  that provide free HIV testing  and  link patients to care and resources. Ryan White grant programs are audited annually for program integrity both internally and by the funding source.

answer_as_filed:
The Ryan White  Part A program at the Ohio State University Infectious Diseases clinic uses 340B savings to provide a variety of services to the community including: 
-Transportation to improve access and adherence to appointments.
- Basic cell phones for patients with identified health disparities to allow for communication with clinic staff, physicians, and pharmacists. This service has improved access, reduced no shows, and enhanced medication adherence.
- Physician & pharmacist staffing effort to allow more time with patients with complex needs. 
- Patient navigation to assist patients maintain adherence to their treatment goals.
- Benefit navigation to help patients access services they may be eligible to obtain (e.g., Medicaid, Medicare). 
- Access to non-perishables for patients with acute nutrition needs.
- Prescription coverage  for patients unable to pay for medications.

answer_as_filed: Ryan White Part A grant funding provides medications and outpatient medical care to uninsured patients in designated high-need areas. Patients currently enrolled in the Ryan White program are eligible for medication assistance, transportation vouchers, as well as medical, lab, dental and psychosocial services provided by staff supported by program income from 340B revenue. Part A grant funds and limited program income are used to  provide access to prescription drugs purchased at 340B discount cost to stretch scarce resources and remove barriers to medication compliance and improve patient quality of life and outcomes. Ryan White grant programs are audited annually for program integrity both internally and by the funding source.

answer_as_filed: Knox Community Hospital uses 340B funds to keep our doors open.  We use the funds to supplement the budget our Case Management department has to assist patients in paying for medications and durrable medical equipment.  We use it to pay our staff so that we can continue to safely care for our patients.  Since 2020, our facility has been in a financial decline.  We have seen an increase in uncompensated care. answer_as_filed: The Ohio Department of Rehabilitation & Correction (ODRC) is an established STD Clinic. Services provided include STD blood testing and screening  for all ODRC incarcerated persons upon arrival into the prison system, as well as STD treatment as clinically indicated. STD education is provided by clinical staff upon ODRC entry, during clinical appointments, during annual physicals, during annual health fairs, prior to community reentry,  and upon patient request. When an incarcerated person on STD treatment is being released back into the community, a 30-day supply of medications is given upon release and community linkage is provided through the Ohio Department of Health. Specific infectious disease nursing duties are assigned at the institutions' medical departments to closely monitor STD patients' care. An annual infectious disease symposium is conducted for ODRC clinical staff and law enforcement partners featuring infection control topics/experts.

answer_as_filed: The Stark County Health Department received federal Title X funding through the Ohio Department of Health Family Planning Program to support essential reproductive health services. As part of this program, the department operated as a 340B covered entity, allowing it to access medications at significantly reduced costs, including utilizing the Ohio Department of Health STI program.  This designation enabled the clinic to stretch limited resources and expand access to care for vulnerable populations. Utilizing 340B pricing, the Title X clinic was able to purchase contraceptives and related medications for STI treatment at a discounted rate or free. These medications were then provided free of charge to uninsured and underinsured clients in accordance with Title X program guidelines and ODH STI program rules and regulations.
